February 1 turns unpaid tax delinquent, and because the lien follows the house, it must be cleared or arranged before a sale.

Collectors add a 6 percent penalty with 1 percent interest, then another percent each month, with the penalty rising to 12 percent in July and interest uncapped. A unit's attorney may add up to 20 percent. A written waiver request is possible in some cases when the tax is paid within three weeks of learning it is late. Schools must carve $140,000 out of a homestead, adding $60,000 for seniors and the disabled, and counties that levy farm-to-market or flood control taxes give $3,000. A frozen school tax amount protects older and disabled owners and can travel proportionally to a later Texas homestead. A mid-year buyer can claim the exemption for what remains of the year when the seller had none. Veterans with a service disability can receive $5,000 to $12,000 off, and a 100 percent rating brings a total homestead exemption.

What if tenants live in my San Angelo house?

A tenant can stay through a sale, but a buyer who wants vacant possession needs the landlord to complete a Texas eviction first.

Absent a different lease term, three days of written notice come first, then a justice court filing. The hearing lands 10 to 21 days later, with the tenant served four days ahead. County court appeals must be filed within five days of judgment, and a constable posts 24 hours' notice before enforcing a writ that cannot issue until six days after judgment.

Who can sign for an inherited San Angelo house?

First learn whether the owner left a will, since that determines which court paper the buyer's closer will ask for.

Texas lets heirs offer a will for probate until four years after death, usually in the owner's home county. When the only debts are real estate liens, a muniment of title can pass the house to heirs, with the order and will filed where the land is. The small estate affidavit is for estates with no will or administration and no more than $75,000 outside the homestead. An heirship affidavit is just a sworn statement that outsiders may decline.

  • See a probate lawyer before signing a purchase contract.

What if I am facing foreclosure in San Angelo?

A Texas power-of-sale foreclosure runs on a fixed clock, so selling beforehand is the way to keep any equity.

A default notice opens a 20 day window to reinstate by paying the arrears. The sale notice follows at least three weeks before an auction held on a first Tuesday in the area the commissioners court has designated. Temple was born as a railroad town. The city's own history says Jonathan Ewing Moore sold 181 acres at $27 an acre to the Santa Fe, and a land auction on June 29, 1881 started the town, named for the railroad's chief engineer.

Bell County's history page adds the backdrop. The same page says the Santa Fe hospital became the city's first hospital in 1891, King's Daughters Hospital followed in 1896, and the Santa Fe merged with Scott & White in 1983.

That medical lineage still sets the tone. It also calls Temple the demographic center of Texas, with 84 percent of the state's people within three hours of the city limits. Houses close to the medical campus and to I-35 tend to draw the broadest pool of buyers.

The Census Bureau counts 98,412 people in Temple for July 2025, which is 19.7 percent above its 2020 base. A borrower facing foreclosure has until the first-Tuesday auction, and Texas lets a borrower reinstate by paying the past-due balance within 20 days after the default notice. A landlord needs written notice to vacate, which is three days unless the lease sets another period, before filing in justice court.

With the Bell County Clerk, because the clerk of the county holding the land keeps deed records. The clerk's manual requires the owner's signature plus a notary's acknowledgment for recording. Cash deals can wrap in a few weeks if title is clean, since nobody waits on loan approval. A listed sale usually takes longer since the buyer's loan and appraisal set the pace. Title problems such as an unprobated estate or an open lien slow either route.

Who pays the property tax when a Bryan house sells?

Tax for the sale year is normally prorated between the two sides on the settlement statement. Any unpaid year has to be cleared at closing because that lien stays with the land. Ask the Brazos County tax office for the current balance.

Can I sell a Bryan house that is listed on Airbnb?

Yes. Settle your hotel occupancy tax returns first, because Bryan requires owners to report short-term rent monthly or quarterly. Tell any buyer whether bookings already exist for future dates.

Do I need to probate before selling an inherited house in Bryan?

Usually yes, or you need another recorded route to show the heirs' authority. Options include a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit, or an administration. Heirs not named on the deed must also prove interest to the appraisal district for a homestead exemption.

What can I do if a Bryan foreclosure sale is scheduled?

Act before the first Tuesday sale date. You can reinstate within 20 days of the default notice, sell the house, or ask the servicer about other options. Equity left after an auction goes to junior lienholders first, then to you.

Is Leander a good place to sell a house quickly?

Leander is an Austin-area suburb that has kept growing, so a fast sale is realistic, as long as you price against newer homes nearby and settle the tax bill carefully. Sellers pick between a cash purchase as-is and a standard listing, and each trades speed against price.

Neighborhood details change the answer more than the city name does, so confirm your own school district, HOA and utility district before you talk numbers.

How did Leander get its start?

Leander lies on U.S. Highway 183 in southwestern Williamson County and was founded in 1882 after the Austin and Northwestern Railroad passed by nearby Bagdad, according to the Handbook of Texas. Merchants moved to the new townsite when the railroad began selling lots on July 17, 1882.

The town stayed small until subdivisions began to appear in the late 1950s and 1960s. Residents incorporated in 1978, and the same source puts population at 3,398 in 1990 and 7,596 in 2000. The Handbook places it inside the Austin metropolitan area. The practical result for a seller is a mix of older homes near the original townsite and many newer builds, so age and condition vary widely from street to street.

Growth in the roll is a signal that new construction continues, and new homes compete with resale listings. The budget page reminds owners to use the state's Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes tool to see each taxing unit's proposed and adopted rates, and the page gives City Hall's address as 105 North Brushy Street.

What does Leander's tax page say about sales and hotel taxes?

Beyond property tax, the city's tax page prints a combined sales tax rate of 8.25 percent: 6.25 percent to the state, 1 percent to the city and 1 percent to Capital Metro. It lists a hotel occupancy tax of 13 percent, made up of 6 percent state and 7 percent city. These taxes do not apply to a sale of your home, but they matter if you have rented it to short-term guests, because the city's figure tells you what a guest stay carried.

The page also notes that Texas has no personal income tax.

How do Texas exemptions and caps affect a Leander seller?

A buyer's tax bill depends on the exemptions they can claim, so sellers should know the basics.

  • The school district exemption is $140,000 on a principal residence, with $60,000 added for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A homestead's appraised value can rise no more than 10 percent a year for school and other taxes, starting the year after the exemption begins.
  • An over-65 or disabled owner's school tax is frozen at the level of the year they qualified, and the ceiling can carry to a new Texas homestead.

A January-to-December buyer who closes mid-year can claim it right away when the prior owner had none. Sellers who hold a freeze should keep that paperwork if they plan to buy again in Texas.

When are Williamson County taxes due?

Statements go out around October 1. A bill still open on February 1 picks up a six percent penalty plus monthly interest, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

Williamson County's pages list a four-installment schedule with payments on January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31 for eligible owners, and a monthly prepayment option drawn from a card or bank account. Ask the county tax office whether your account qualifies before counting on any plan.

  2. Check for an HOA or utility district transfer fee.
  3. Sign the deed before a notary so the county clerk can record it.
  4. Settle the year's tax share at closing under the contract terms.

An heir selling an inherited home should know the appraisal district asks for an ownership affidavit and a death certificate to keep the exemption in place.

A prepared file speeds a fast sale and avoids price cuts late in the process. Collect the following before you call buyers.

  • Roof, foundation and air conditioning records.
  • The HOA contact and any capital contribution or transfer fee.
  • Your most recent Williamson County tax statement showing each taxing unit.
  • A short written list of known defects.

The Handbook of Texas notes housing subdivisions beginning in the late 1950s, so older houses may need electrical or plumbing updates that a buyer will price in. A cash buyer can skip those repairs, while a buyer with a mortgage may require them.

What local detail should a Leander seller mention to buyers?

Leander's history gives you talking points. The Handbook of Texas says the town was named for a railroad station manager, most likely, rather than the railroad official some county histories credit, and that cotton gins, ranching and cedar fenceposts supported the early economy. A Masonic lodge ran the only free school in the area from 1870 until June 1899, and the Leander High School Association was incorporated on June 27, 1899.

School consolidation brought Pleasant Hill in 1928, Round Mountain and Volente in 1938, and White Stone in 1952. Leander ISD's rate appears on the city's tax page. Buyers with children often ask which school zone a house falls in, so confirm the zoning with the district before listing and put the answer in your marketing.

  • Population grew from 329 in 1890 to 2,700 in 1983.

Have the title company list every closing cost, county recording fees included, before signing day.

Who sets the appraised value of my Leander home?

Williamson County's appraisal district values property on January 1 of each year. Protests are due May 15 unless the notice arrives late, in which case the window runs 30 days from delivery.

What happens to my homestead exemption after I sell?

It ends with your ownership. A buyer who uses the home as a principal residence can apply for their own, and the over-65 freeze may follow an eligible owner to a new Texas homestead.

What is Mission, Texas known for?

Mission is a Hidalgo County city on the Rio Grande, founded in 1908 when the Missouri Pacific Railroad set up a station near the center of a new development. It was named for La Lomita Chapel, and the city's history page says the population is approaching 70,000.

The city describes this area as the place where citrus was first planted in the Rio Grande Valley. The multimillion-dollar citrus industry is celebrated each year at the Texas Citrus Fiesta, each year. For a seller, that heritage is the backdrop to the local housing stock.

  • The historic La Lomita Mission still stands and draws visitors.
  • William Jennings Bryan built a winter home in Mission, and the area appears in Larry McMurtry's Lonesome Dove.
  • Land here began as Spanish porciones that ran about two-thirds of a mile along the river and 11 to 16 miles inland, a pattern recorded in county land records.

Three paths, each with its own timing.

  • Cash buyer. Suits as-is sales, clouded inherited title and storm or roof damage.

Land around Mission began as Spanish porciones, long strips of land along the river. The city's history notes that porciones 55 and 57 held Rancho La Lomita, home of the chapel for which the city is named. Later the Rancho La Lomita Land Company, run by Captain Conway and J.W. Hoit, developed the area, and the railroad station of 1908 anchored the new town.

That history is why older Mission parcels can carry long chains of ownership in county records. A title search follows each link. If your family has held the land for generations, collect any old deeds, family agreements or probate papers you have, because gaps in the chain can slow a sale. A cash buyer's title company can tell you early what it needs.

What does Mission require for building permits and repairs?

Mission's Inspections Division reviews permits for new buildings and checks compliance with minimum building codes. A permit is also required for any concrete or asphalt slab with a value of $100 or more, and mobile homes need permits.

Inspectors check foundation, plumbing, framing, mechanical, A/C, electrical, setbacks, sidewalks and buffering on new residences. Structures that existed before annexation are treated as grandfathered while they stay as they are, but expanding one requires a permit and brings zoning and setback rules into play. The division's phone is 956-580-8691 per the city page. Before you list, ask whether an addition, slab or carport was permitted, since open work can slow a buyer's lender.

Hidalgo CAD values Mission property and takes homestead and over-65 applications through an online portal. Its customer service line is 956-381-8466.

See the Comptroller exemptions page.

What if unpaid taxes lead to a tax sale?

Unpaid taxes become a lien that can be foreclosed. The Comptroller says a lien attaches every January 1 and lets a court seize property even if ownership has changed. Collectors can add court costs, and private attorneys under contract can add up to 20 percent.

If land was sold at a tax sale, redemption rights are narrow. For a homestead, the owner has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed, paying a premium of 25 percent in the first year or 50 percent in the second, plus costs. Other property has 180 days. Former owners have two years to claim excess proceeds. Request a payoff and itemized statement from the tax office before deciding.

  • Over-65 or disabled homeowners may pay delinquent amounts in installments.
  • Some collectors allow plans of up to 36 months, required on a homestead.
  • A waiver of penalty and interest must be asked for in writing.

Line up each offer on the same terms. A high price with a long inspection period can net you less than a lower cash offer that closes promptly.

Ask for the final numbers on a closing statement. If anything looks unclear, ask the title company, not the buyer, to explain it.

How do liens, probate and foreclosure play out in Mission?

Liens and taxes come out of proceeds at closing. For an inherited house, expect the title company to ask for orders or recorded papers naming who may sign. Wills must be probated within four years of death.

A lender usually forecloses by nonjudicial auction on a first Tuesday, with notice 21 days ahead. A deficiency suit must follow within two years. Selling first keeps equity with you. The State Law Library foreclosure guide explains the stages.

With the clerk of the county where the land lies, after notarized signature. The 2023 clerk manual lists $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages plus capped records fees. Verify the current figures with the clerk.

Ask who the purchaser is, whether the offer is as-is, and where earnest money sits. Ask what closing date they propose and what happens if a title problem appears. Read the contract in full before signing, and make sure the title company, not the buyer, prepares your closing statement.

Yes, to cash buyers who price in the repairs. Listing usually means fixing damage for lender approval.

For any slab worth $100 or more. Expanding an older structure also needs a permit and brings zoning setbacks into play.

Who sets appraised values in Mission?

The Hidalgo County Appraisal District. Reach customer service at 956-381-8466 or use its portal for homestead and over-65 filings.

A muniment of title, administration or a transfer on death deed. A will must be probated within four years of death.

Can selling halt a foreclosure?

If closing happens before the auction, yes. Texas allows 20 days to reinstate after the default notice and at least 21 days' notice of sale.

Which selling routes make sense for a Baytown homeowner in a hurry?

A Baytown owner can hire an agent, go it alone, or hand the house to a cash buyer who accepts whatever condition it is in. Cash deals draw owners with a repair backlog, a property that came through an estate, a tenant situation they want to end, or a lender or court deadline.

Baytown had about 86,561 residents in mid-2025, and the 2020-2024 estimates say owners occupy 52.3 percent of homes. With a middle home value of $197,300, a long repair list can eat a big slice of what a listing would bring.

  • Hiring an agent: best for a sound house when you have time for open houses and loan approval.
  • Doing it yourself: you handle price, contract and buyer questions yourself, then close at a title company.
  • Cash buyer: no lender, no repair demands, and a closing date set after a short walk-through.

What turned a ferry crossing and an oil field into Baytown?

Baytown owes its shape to the refinery. The Handbook of Texas calls it a highly industrialized city of oil refining, rubber, chemical and carbon black plants, thirty miles east of downtown Houston on Interstate 10 and State Highway 146.

The area was isolated farmland until a 1908 oil strike beside Tabbs Bay. The nearby Goose Creek field became, in 1916, the first offshore drilling in Texas, and in 1917 the founders of Humble Oil and Refining bought about 2,200 acres for a refinery, with construction starting in 1919. The company laid out streets, supplied utilities, sold lots and financed employee homes, and the camp of tents and shacks became permanent in 1923. Pelly, Goose Creek and the Baytown site then merged, and the city was established on January 24, 1948.

Residents numbered 20,958 in 1948 and 67,117 in 1990, as the city stretched from 7.5 to more than 32 square miles. By the 2020 Census the land area was 37.00 square miles. A tunnel under the Houston Ship Channel opened in 1953 and gave way to the Fred Hartman Bridge in the mid-1990s. The Handbook lists Lee College and more than ten major petrochemical plants among the local institutions. Because the company financed employee homes in the 1920s, parts of the city started as company-supported housing, and buyers of older homes will ask about age, plumbing and foundation.

The older layers run deep. A ferry crossing at the junction of the San Jacinto River and Buffalo Bayou, set up in 1822, still operates, and a grant of more than 9,000 acres in 1824 covered most of present Baytown. The boundaries now run from near the San Jacinto River east into Chambers County and include former communities such as Cedar Bayou and Wooster.

Which county handles my Baytown property, Harris or Chambers?

It depends on the parcel. Baytown sits in southeastern Harris County and reaches east into Chambers County, so two sets of county offices serve the city.

The split decides who files your deed, who values the lot and who sends the bill. Look in the wrong county and your parcel simply will not show.

  • Read the top of your tax bill for the county and the account number.
  • Ask the closing agent which clerk will file the deed.
  • If you live near the county line, check which school and other districts show on the bill.

The Comptroller's property tax basics page says appraisal districts value property as of January 1 and bills go out around October 1.

Are nightly rentals allowed in Baytown, and does that affect a buyer?

Baytown's land development code has allowed nightly rentals in residential and mixed-use districts only with a Special Use Permit voted by City Council. The first request reached Council on December 11, 2025, and was approved with conditions for an existing house in a Suburban Residential district.

Staff then drafted a text amendment that would replace the permit vote with a standard permit process in those districts. A Planning and Zoning hearing was set for March 17, 2026, and a City Council hearing for April 23, 2026. Council also looked at annual permits and inspections and at limits on occupancy and parking.

If your house has hosted paying guests, ask Baytown planning staff which rule covers the address and whether any approval exists. A buyer counting on rental income should verify the status with the city before signing. The city's amendment notice describes the proposal.

What are the steps for selling a house left to me in Baytown?

Work out how title reaches you, since that decides what the insurer will accept. A will can be probated within four years of death, and a court may take a later filing for good reason.

  • Muniment of title: for an estate whose only debts are real-estate liens; the court order and will go to the clerk where the land sits.
  • Small estate affidavit: limited to $75,000 in assets outside the homestead, and generally no real property apart from a homestead passing to a spouse or minor children.
  • Affidavit of heirship: a sworn statement that no law forces a title company to take.
  • Executor's or administrator's deed: follows a court appointment.

Heirs missing from the recorded deed give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill to keep a homestead exemption. The State Law Library's informal probate guide explains each path, and a probate lawyer can say which fits.

What happens to back taxes when a Baytown house sells?

Each year's tax lien attaches on January 1 and rides with the house, so any unpaid amount is taken from your sale money when you close. Bills are mailed in October, and accounts open on February 1 turn delinquent with a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

A homestead owner who has fallen behind can ask the collector about a payment plan, and some collectors offer up to 36 months. Penalty and interest may be waived in narrow cases if the tax is paid within 21 days of learning of the delinquency and a written request is made inside 181 days. Request a payoff number before choosing a closing date, and have the title company check for judgment liens.

Is Baytown in Harris or Chambers County?

Both. The city lies in southeastern Harris County and extends east into western Chambers County. Your tax bill names the county, which fixes where the deed is filed and which appraisal district values the lot.

Can I tell a buyer my Baytown house works as a nightly rental?

Only after checking with the city. Baytown has required a Special Use Permit approved by City Council, and a 2026 amendment proposed a permit process instead. Planning staff can say which rule applies to your address.

Is there a time limit to probate a will before I sell?

A will generally must be filed within four years of death, although a court can accept a later filing for good cause. A muniment of title order and the will then go to the clerk of the county where the property sits.

Why do Mansfield houses sell the way they do?

Mansfield sits between Fort Worth and Dallas, and its housing is mostly recent suburban construction. A seller with a dated floor plan is competing with new houses a few streets away, so repairs and asking price do most of the work in deciding how long a sale takes.

An estimated 84,444 people lived in Mansfield as of July 1, 2025, per the Census Bureau, a 16.3 percent gain over the 2020 base. Younger families set the tone: 28.4 percent of residents are under 18 and households average 3.04 people. Bedroom count, yard size and school zone come up early in nearly every showing.

  • Putting the house on the market through an agent exposes it to the most buyers, though weekend showings and inspection repair requests come with it.

How much do Mansfield homes cost, and who lives in them?

Mansfield is mid-priced for North Texas. Census estimates for 2020-2024 show a 71.5 percent ownership rate and $410,700 as the middle value for an owned home.

Which counties and highways does Mansfield straddle?

Mansfield spreads across three counties: mostly Tarrant, with pieces in Johnson and Ellis. Where your lot falls decides which office bills the taxes and which clerk files the deed.

The Texas State Historical Association puts the city center about fifteen miles southeast of Fort Worth and twenty-two miles southwest of Dallas. U.S. Route 287 and Texas Highway 360 serve it, and 360 ends in southern Mansfield.

What shaped Mansfield's economy and neighborhoods?

The town began as Walnut Creek and took its name from a steam mill built in 1857 by Ralph Man and Julian Feild. The railroad came in 1886, and the town incorporated on August 23, 1890.

Best Maid Pickles built a pickling plant here, and the state named Mansfield its Pickle Capital in 2013. Industrial parks in the 1960s and a can plant that opened in 1969 pulled the economy from farming toward manufacturing. The Handbook of Texas lists Mouser Electronics, Methodist Mansfield Medical Center and Klein Tools as the top employers in 2021.

Population stood at 28,031 in 2000, 56,368 in 2010 and 72,602 in 2020. The old downtown corridor survives, along with the Man House Museum, and a Historic Landmark Commission recommends sites for preservation. An owner of an older home near downtown should ask the city whether any historic designation touches the property before setting a price.

What are Mansfield's schools and parks like for buyers?

Public schools belong to Mansfield Independent School District. The Handbook reports 35,524 students in 2021-22 across twenty-five elementary schools, eight intermediate schools, seven middle schools, five traditional high schools and four alternative campuses.

City parks include Elmer W. Oliver Nature Park, a dog park, many athletic fields and the Walnut Creek Linear Trail, which is planned to run the length of town. Private venues such as Hawaiian Falls, Big League Dreams and the Mansfield National Golf Course add to the draw. A listing that names the nearest campuses and trail access answers questions buyers already have. Confirm zoning with the district before advertising a campus.

How is Mansfield run, and what does the Census say about its economy?

Mansfield uses a council-manager form of government, with a mayor and six council members who each represent the whole city. The Handbook of Texas says the city staff numbered more than 500 as of 2022, the library dates to 1929, the police department was organized in 1954 and the fire department runs five stations.

The Census Bureau counts 4,312 veterans and a foreign-born share of 13.6 percent. Among residents age five and up, 18.8 percent speak another language at home, and 96.2 percent of households have broadband. Retail sales reached $1,430,594 thousand in 2022, or $18,642 per person, while clinics, hospitals and social services took in $966,319 thousand.

The poverty rate is 5.8 percent, and 12.6 percent of residents under 65 have no health insurance. These figures describe a stable middle-income suburb, which is the buyer pool most Mansfield listings aim for.

Can a Mansfield house be a short-term rental?

Not by default. The city says short-term rentals, meaning stays under 30 days, are not permitted in residential areas of Mansfield unless the property gets approval first. Listing a house online does not make the use legal.

Approval comes through a zoning change to a Planned Development, and the city states that approval is not guaranteed. Most applications take about 90 to 120 days from submittal to a final decision, with review by staff, the Planning and Zoning Commission and the City Council.

  • The application fee is $2,500, plus $100 per acre or part of an acre.
  • The file must include a site plan with parking, a floor plan with exits, proof of insurance and Hotel Occupancy Tax registration.
  • The owner also lists house rules, the maximum number of occupants and whether the home will be owner occupied.

Why does this affect a sale? A house that has been used as a vacation rental without approval can carry a compliance problem, and a buyer who wants rental income should ask the Planning Department what the property is entitled to do.

How are deeds recorded in Mansfield, and what do clerks charge?

A Mansfield sale may involve the Tarrant, Johnson or Ellis county clerk, whichever covers your parcel. Before a clerk will record a conveyance of land, it needs a signature plus an acknowledgment from a notary or comparable officer, or an oath before two witnesses.

The 2023 clerk manual from Texas Courts lists $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after it, with records management, archive and technology fees stacked on top. Totals vary by county, so phone the clerk for what your deed will cost.

  • Some commissioners courts waive recording fees for buyers using certain grant programs.

Which taxes follow a Mansfield house to closing?

The county tax office, not the appraisal district, collects the bill, so ask the Tarrant, Johnson or Ellis office for your account balance. An unpaid earlier year travels with the house to the next owner, and the sale year's tax is split at closing.

Yes. Cash buyers purchase in present condition, whereas a retail buyer usually negotiates repairs after the inspection. Weigh the money you walk away with, not only the offer.

Look at the legal description or tax statement. The city lies mostly in Tarrant County with parts in Johnson and Ellis, and the clerk where your parcel sits records the deed.

$410,700, per the 2020-2024 estimates. Age, size and condition can put a given house well off that midpoint.

Mansfield Independent School District, created in 1909. Ask the district for current campus zones before you advertise a particular school.

Which sale route works for a Longview owner in a hurry?

Owners in Longview with a deadline generally choose between a listing, a private sale and a cash purchase that leaves the repairs to the buyer. A listing reaches the most buyers. A cash sale closes sooner when repairs, liens, tenants or an estate stand in the way.

The city is the seat of Gregg County, along Interstate 20 and U.S. highways 80 and 259, roughly 125 miles east of Dallas. It extends across the line into Harrison County, so the parcel's county decides which appraisal district and which clerk handle your paperwork.

  • Confirm the county from your deed or tax bill before you request offers.
  • Collect the deed, any mortgage payoff statement and the latest tax bill.
  • Set any cash offer beside the likely proceeds of a listing, minus repairs, commission and months of upkeep.

What does Longview's railroad and oilfield past mean for its houses?

Longview began in the early 1870s when the Southern Pacific, later the Texas and Pacific, extended track westward and platted a town a mile west of the older settlement of Earpville. The Handbook of Texas records incorporation on May 17, 1871, making it the first community in Gregg County to incorporate.

The East Texas oilfield discovery in the early 1930s kept Longview out of the worst of the Depression. The same entry says the population more than doubled in that decade, and postwar annexation of Greggton and Spring Hill pushed the total toward 62,762 by 1980.

That boom left a large stock of mid-century homes. Buyers inspecting them focus on roofs, foundations, old wiring and plumbing, so a seller of an older Longview house should expect repair requests.

Which industries and school districts shape demand in Longview?

The city grew from a cotton, lumber and railroad town into an industrial and medical center. The Handbook of Texas points to the Big Inch pipeline, which began at Longview in 1942 and carried crude oil east through 1945, a plant making earth-moving equipment, and a chemical complex that became the largest in inland Texas.

It also describes Longview, Pine Tree and Spring Hill independent school districts, each with a major high school, as serving the area when the entry was written. A buyer's school search often decides which neighborhoods get shown first, and the district also sets part of the tax bill.

Other postwar landmarks in the Handbook include Gregg County Airport, Lake Cherokee and the conversion of a wartime hospital complex into LeTourneau Technical Institute, and Texas Eastman came to a site near Longview in 1950. For decades the Kelly Plow Company, a farm-equipment factory open from 1882 until after World War II, was the main plant. The Handbook also notes a new county courthouse in 1932, paid for by oil-boom tax receipts.

Steady industrial and medical employers bring relocating workers, though demand follows oil and manufacturing cycles. A house in a sought-after district may sell on the open market, while one with deferred maintenance may suit a cash buyer.

Which office appraises a Longview house?

The Gregg County Appraisal District values real and business personal property in that county under the Texas Property Tax Code. Parcels on the Harrison side belong to that county's appraisal district, so check your tax statement for the office that applies.

Gregg's district announced a residential reappraisal running from July 2026 to March 2027, with exterior inspections and new photographs. Appraisers carry a pictured ID, a business card and a state registration card, and leave a door hanger and card when no one is home.

For a homestead exemption, the district lists three conditions: you hold title and use the home as your residence on the filing date, no spouse claims a residence homestead elsewhere, and you present a Texas license or state ID showing the same address. Its taxpayer liaison is at 4367 W Loop 281 in Longview, and the number it lists is 903-238-8823.

How does the Texas tax calendar play out for a Longview seller?

Longview owners follow the statewide calendar. Value and the tax lien are fixed on January 1, a protest deadline lands in mid-May, and bills go out about October 1. Late January is the last safe payment date for a Longview bill, and the Gregg district's reappraisal visits mean a new photo of your house may be on file by spring, and from February 1 a collector adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

  • School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, with a further $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.
  • Disabled veterans receive tiered partial exemptions, and a 100 percent rating can mean a total exemption on the homestead.
  • Heirs missing from a recorded deed can submit an ownership affidavit to the district to claim the exemption.

At a sale, the title company divides the year's bill between buyer and seller. An open lien gets a payoff request and is cleared from your proceeds.

What can a Longview owner do about foreclosure or unpaid taxes?

Call the lender or tax office before a deadline, since both processes move on fixed steps. A Texas deed of trust lets a lender sell without a court, but only after a default notice with a twenty-day cure period and a sale notice three weeks ahead of an auction held early in a month.

Afterward, a lender may sue for a shortfall within two years. Redemption is narrow: for tax sales, a Texas Supreme Court opinion on the court system's site describes two years for homestead, farm or mineral property and 180 days for other land.

Closing a sale before the auction often leaves an owner better off than the auction price would. Have the payoff amounts and lien balances put in writing by the title company.

How are inherited and rented Longview houses handled?

Begin with the deed. Should the owner have passed away, work out whether probate is needed: a will can be probated for four years after death, and a muniment of title can pass real estate where the estate owes nothing beyond real-estate liens.

For a rented house, expect three days' written notice, a justice court filing, service on the tenant four days ahead of trial and a writ of possession six days after judgment. Because of that schedule, many owners sell while the renter is still living there.

Where does a Longview deed get recorded?

The clerk of Gregg or Harrison County keeps the records, depending on where the land lies. The signature needs a notary's acknowledgment, and the clerk can quote current charges. Closing funds usually cover them. Longview owners should also check that the legal description matches the deed already of record.

Is a Longview house in Gregg or Harrison County?

Either, because the city crosses the county line. The appraisal district on your tax bill is the office to contact, and the clerk of that same county records the deed.

Can a lien stop a Longview sale?

No, though it must be paid. The title company requests payoff figures and settles liens from your proceeds, and a buyer cannot receive clear title while delinquent property taxes remain.

When are Longview property taxes late?

Most unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1. A six percent penalty and one percent interest apply then, and the penalty grows monthly until July 1.

Must I repair a Longview house before a cash sale?

No. A cash buyer purchases as-is, with the price reflecting the work expected. Compare the offer against a repaired-and-listed price before deciding.

How quickly can foreclosure move in Texas?

Fast. A default notice gives twenty days to cure, a sale notice must come three weeks before the auction, and sales happen monthly. Talk to the lender early.

Homes here are modestly priced, with a $121,900 Census midpoint for 2020 to 2024. At that level, a repair bill of a few thousand dollars eats a big share of the price, so owners of older, damaged or inherited houses often weigh a direct sale against fixing up first.

How did Pharr grow into the city it is today?

The city lies east of McAllen in south central Hidalgo County. According to the state historical handbook, John Connally Kelley and Louisiana sugarcane grower Henry N. Pharr became co-owners of 16,000 acres in 1909, and Kelley's townsite company laid out the town in his partner's name.

The sugar plantation failed, yet the irrigation system kept vegetable and cotton farms supplied. Pharr incorporated in 1916, took on a commission government in 1949, and in 1956 voters rejected merging with McAllen. The PSJA school district was formed in 1919 with San Juan and Alamo.

Counts rose from 4,784 in 1940 to 32,921 in 1990 and 70,400 in 2010. The handbook credits McAllen's growth, annexed colonias, a young population and winter visitors, and says the Pharr-Reynosa International Bridge, opened in 1994, made Pharr a major port of entry. Census estimates now show 80,830 people on 23.63 square miles.

Early figures show a slow start: about 600 people in 1915, 1,560 in 1920 and 3,225 by 1931, when the town had 105 businesses. By the 1960s local factories made irrigation equipment, clay products, mattresses, harvesting machinery and concrete products, so the city has long been more than a farm market.

Does the international bridge support Pharr's housing market?

It underpins the job base, and jobs drive housing demand. The bridge's own page cites about 175,000 vehicle crossings a month, over 120,000 of them commercial trucks, and calls it Hidalgo County's only full-service commercial crossing.

It also ranks Pharr third nationally for trade with Mexico after Laredo and El Paso, and first for produce. Census data lists $515,641,000 in transportation and warehousing receipts for 2022, which fits that picture of trucking, storage and customs work.

Workers in those jobs may prefer homes near freight routes, and the average drive to work is 21.1 minutes. If your house is close to major roads or the bridge approach, tell buyers.

The bridge page also describes a planned second span with four more lanes, a new freight access road and more than $35 million in city-funded improvements aimed at 2023. That target year has passed, so ask the city for the current status of the expansion if a buyer asks how it may affect traffic near your street.

The page cites more than $41 billion in global trade moving through the crossing, with imports and exports both growing during the pandemic. Those totals describe the freight economy, not home prices, so use them as background and not as a promise of appreciation.

Price to Pharr's own market. With a $121,900 median value and a $52,814 median household income, price sensitivity is high, so a clean inspection matters more than extras. Fix visible leaks, broken windows and electrical hazards first, since an inspector will find them.

If the house needs more work than you can fund, a direct sale as-is avoids the cost of repairs and the wait for a buyer's loan.

What Hidalgo County tax rules affect a Pharr seller?

Unpaid tax stays with a Texas house because the lien attaches every January 1. The Hidalgo County tax office can give a payoff figure for the closing table.

Bills come around October 1 and go delinquent after January 31. Attorney fees of up to 20 percent may be stacked on that.

  • Veterans with a disability rating: $5,000 to $12,000, rising to a full homestead exemption at 100 percent.
  • Protests: file by May 15, or within 30 days of the notice if that falls later.

The Comptroller adds that a veteran who missed April 30 can still apply under Section 11.22 for up to five years after the delinquency date.

How does recording work when a Pharr house is sold?

The deed is filed at the Hidalgo County Clerk's office. Before that, you sign it with a notary present.

A family house with no recorded deed needs extra proof of ownership. An affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement, and a title company is free to refuse it, so some buyers ask for a court order.

What if the Pharr house faces foreclosure or an estate dispute?

Dates come first. Once a default notice arrives, you have 20 days to cure the arrears, and the lender owes 21 days' warning before a first-Tuesday auction.

For an estate, the usual window to probate a will is four years from death, and a small estate affidavit can fit when assets are $75,000 or less apart from the homestead.

At the Hidalgo County Clerk, where Pharr lies. The seller signs before a notary, and the title company handles the filing.

Most of the town is served by Lewisville ISD and Argyle ISD, and Denton ISD, Grapevine-Colleyville ISD and Northwest ISD cover small areas. The town counts 16 elementary, 8 middle and 5 high schools serving residents, so check the district against your exact address.

Does Flower Mound regulate short-term rentals?

Yes. The town requires short-term rentals to register through a platform run by GovOS and to remit a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax, with registration opening November 20, 2023 and tax collection starting December 1, 2023.

Tax forms and payments are due on the 15th of the month after the occupancy, even when no tax was collected. A person who has not paid by the 25th owes a 15 percent penalty, and delinquent tax draws interest at 10 percent per year 30 days after the due date. Operators may keep a 1 percent collection fee if they pay on time.

  • Questions: the town's short-term rental email address.

If the house was an Airbnb-style rental, close the account and pay any final month's tax before the sale.

How do homestead exemptions and the tax freeze work in Flower Mound?

School districts in Texas must grant a $140,000 homestead exemption, and a senior or disabled owner receives an extra $60,000 from school districts. Any taxing unit may adopt a local exemption of a fifth of value at most, with a floor of $5,000, so check the exemptions your taxing units have adopted with the appraisal district.

State law also caps yearly growth in a homestead's appraised value to 10 percent, beginning the year after the exemption is first granted. Seniors and disabled owners get a school tax ceiling, and part of it can follow the owner to a replacement Texas homestead. A buyer purchasing after January 1 can usually claim the exemption for the remaining months of that year when the seller never held it.

Ask the appraisal district which exemptions are on file for your house, since a missing one can be worth claiming before you sell.

What happens if property tax on a Flower Mound house is behind?

The tax lien that attaches each January 1 stays with the property, so back taxes get paid at or before closing. Waiting adds cost, because late charges step up through the early months of the year. Anything unpaid on February 1 picks up a 6 percent charge and monthly interest of 1 percent, and the charge reaches 12 percent from July 1.

A taxing unit's collection attorney may tack on as much as a fifth of the tax. A homeowner may ask in writing for a waiver of penalty and interest, generally paying the tax within 21 days of learning of the delinquency and asking before the 181st day after delinquency. Some collectors allow payment plans of up to 36 months on a residence homestead.

If the property goes to a tax sale, redemption rights depend on the property type and the statute, and homestead land has a two-year redemption window. Get the county tax office's payoff number before saying yes to any offer.

Age is spread evenly. The 55 to 64 bracket is the largest at 15.8 percent, and children under 15 make up 19.3 percent of the population, which helps explain steady interest in family-sized houses near schools.

Whatever offer you take, read the closing statement line by line before you sign. A figure you do not recognize is worth a call to the title company, because errors are easiest to fix before funds move. Ask for the final numbers a day or two ahead so you have time to compare them with the contract. If a buyer asks you to leave appliances, window coverings or a storage shed, write that into the contract so nothing is left to memory.

How do I record the sale of a Flower Mound house?

The title company can tell you which county clerk handles the parcel. That office also keeps the liens and releases a title search turns up, and it files the new deed once a notary has acknowledged the signature.

Fees are set by the clerk, so ask for a quote before closing day.

Before you sign, confirm that the loan payoff, the current year's tax share and any short-term rental tax account are all settled on the closing statement, and keep a copy of every recorded document for your files.

Buyers tend to be well informed. With a town-reported $166,219 median household income and 65.2 percent of homes valued at $500,000 or more, so pricing and condition decide the speed.

Yes. Short-term rentals register through the town's GovOS portal and remit a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax, with returns due on the 15th of the following month.

Which schools serve Flower Mound?

Lewisville ISD and Argyle ISD serve most of the town, with Denton, Grapevine-Colleyville and Northwest ISDs covering small areas.

What penalty applies to late Texas property tax?

Late charges begin on February 1 and step up on July 1. A collection attorney's fee can then be added.

Can I keep my homestead exemption when I sell?

It stays with you only while you live there. A buyer applies for their own after closing and may get it for the remainder of that tax year if the prior owner did not receive it.

Which ways of selling a Cedar Park house are open to me?

A Cedar Park owner can work with an agent, manage the sale personally, or accept an investor's cash purchase with no repairs. Condition and timing decide which suits you.

Three Cedar Park items surface in nearly every sale: the permit record, any short-term rental registration, and the tax account.

How did Cedar Park grow from a railroad stop into a city?

Cedar Park grew from a ranch settlement into an Austin suburb that was incorporated in 1973. The Texas Historical Commission marker, dedicated in 1985 and set outside the public library at 550 Discovery Blvd., tells it: in 1873 a couple bought a large tract rich in cedar and limestone, a post office opened in 1874 under the name Running Brushy, and the railroad arrived in 1882 when the name changed to Bruggerhoff. Five years later the present name was adopted.

The marker adds that the founder opened a cedar yard to sell posts as barbed wire spread, that the early twentieth century brought little growth, and that by 1960 nearly all traces of the old community had disappeared. Austin's growth in the 1970s pulled people north. The city's economic development group now calls Cedar Park the third largest city in the Austin metro and a part of Williamson County.

Which appraisal district and county handle my Cedar Park property taxes?

Your latest tax statement names the county and the appraisal district that carry your parcel. Cedar Park describes itself as part of Williamson County, whose Central Appraisal District values property there.

Texas levies no state property tax, so each local unit sets its own rate. Appraised values are set on January 1, a lien for that year attaches the same day, and bills follow in October. Per the Comptroller, a penalty and interest begin to build once tax goes delinquent on February 1.

For current rates, call the Williamson County tax office and request the adopted figure for each unit on your bill.

How do the homestead exemption and the 10 percent cap work in Cedar Park?

Cedar Park homeowners get a brake on rising assessments, and the brake stays with the owner rather than the house. Williamson CAD says a home qualifies in the second full year the exemption has been on the property for the same owner, and that increases in existing assessed value are held to 10 percent a year even when market value climbs faster.

The district also says the cap does not transfer with ownership, so a buyer starts fresh and may see a bigger jump than you did. Useful points from the district:

  • You apply once; the exemption stays unless you move or add another one.
  • A Texas driver license or ID showing your current address is required.
  • Processing can take up to 90 days.
  • The chief appraiser re-checks each homestead exemption within every five tax years.

What does Cedar Park's short-term rental registration mean for sellers?

If your Cedar Park house is rented for stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, City Council's April 2026 ordinance applies. Registration became required on October 1, 2026, costs $100 a year, and ties into Hotel Occupancy Tax reporting under Chapter 10 of the City Code. The city estimates about 200 active short-term rentals.

A buyer who plans to keep renting will ask whether the registration exists and whether tax was remitted. The city lists Development Services at 512-401-5100 for registration and Utility Billing at 512-401-5300 for hotel tax payments, and registered owners can watch remittance through an online portal. The city says registration exists so it can count and locate these rentals, support safety, and make sure the hotel tax is collected. Gather the confirmation and remittance history before you list, because they are the first things a rental buyer asks to see.

What if the Cedar Park house is inherited, in foreclosure or has a tenant?

Each situation runs on a Texas clock.

  • Foreclosure: the borrower gets 20 days from the default notice to reinstate, and auctions take place at the courthouse on first Tuesdays.
  • Inheritance: a will can be probated for four years after death, and the small estate affidavit tops out at $75,000 excluding homestead and exempt property.
  • Tenant: a landlord normally gives 3 days of written notice to vacate before filing in justice court, unless the lease sets another period.

A buyer can take on these issues, but the title company still needs proof of who may sign. A Williamson County probate attorney can say which paper fits.

What should I do first if I want to sell my Cedar Park house quickly?

Five checks, done in order, show you which sale routes are realistically open to you.

  • Pull the tax statement and confirm the district and any balance.
  • Ask Development Services whether any permit on the address is open.
  • Get your mortgage payoff figure.
  • If the house was a short-term rental, collect registration and hotel tax records.
  • Name your deadline, such as a sale date or a move, and tell every buyer you talk to about it.

More questions about Cedar Park, TX

Can I sell my Cedar Park house with an open building permit?

Yes, though it complicates the sale. A Cedar Park permit lapses after 180 days without a start or with work stopped. Call Development Services at 512-401-5100 about the record, or sell to a buyer willing to take the open item.

Must my Cedar Park short-term rental be registered before a sale?

If guests stay 30 days or fewer, registration has been required since October 1, 2026, at $100 a year. A buyer planning to keep renting will want the registration and your hotel occupancy tax records.

Does my homestead tax cap pass to the buyer?

No. Williamson CAD states the cap does not transfer with ownership. The new owner applies for an exemption of their own, and the cap counts from their first full year.

When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?

Tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent on February 1, per the Texas Comptroller. For the exact balance on your account, call the Williamson County tax office.

What does the Texas foreclosure timeline look like?

A default notice starts a 20-day reinstatement window. After that, the lender gives notice of sale, and the auction happens at the courthouse on a first Tuesday.

Manufacturers added jobs after the war, making goods such as furniture, plastics, lighting fixtures and tortillas by 1980. The same source records growth from 12,713 residents in 1962 to 18,860 in 1972, and 34,733 in 2000.

QuickFacts gives the later picture: 44,894 in the 2010 Census and 67,553 in 2020. Growth that fast leaves a wide range of housing, from older homes near downtown to newer construction on the edges, so describe your house's age, systems and lot when you talk to buyers.

How did San Marcos grow into a college and commuter town?

Settlement gathered around the San Marcos Springs. Hays County was organized March 1, 1848, with San Marcos as its seat and 387 residents. The International-Great Northern Railroad arrived on August 31, 1880, and the 1880s decade lifted the population to 2,335.

A state normal school was chartered in 1899 and opened in 1903 as Southwest Texas State Normal School, later growing into Southwest Texas State University. The district's hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, and the phone number is (512) 268-2522. After August 7 of each year, Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes links to a local database showing the tax each unit would levy under its proposed rate, and owners can subscribe to alerts there.

The district also appraises through the year. Staff walk neighborhoods and commercial areas to measure new construction and update property details, so an addition you built without telling anyone can surface in your value. Make sure your records match the house a buyer will see.

The county clerk where the parcel sits files the deed, after a notary or similar officer witnesses the signature. Fees in the Texas courts manual start at $5.00 for page one and add $4.00 per extra page.

Under the Comptroller's calendar, values are set on January 1, the day the year's tax lien attaches, so taxes follow the property through a sale. Owners who want to contest a value generally have until mid-May.

Does a delinquent tax bill or foreclosure change my options?

Yes, and both put a clock on a sale. Under the Comptroller's payment page, unpaid taxes are delinquent after January 31 and a six percent penalty plus one percent interest begins on February 1. Interest keeps running at one percent a month.

For a mortgage in default, the State Law Library explains that a homeowner has 20 days after the default notice to catch up, and the lender must then post a sale notice three weeks ahead. Sales are on the first Tuesday of each month. A cash sale that closes ahead of that date can leave you with whatever equity exists instead of a foreclosure on your record.

A payoff for back taxes or a lender balance is deducted from your proceeds, so get the exact figures from the escrow officer before you accept a price.

Which nets more in Missouri City, cash or a listing?

Listing means commissions, repairs, carrying costs and time, while a cash sale usually means a lower price and little else. Which wins depends on the house and your deadline.

  • Listing: pay for repairs, cleaning, staging and months of mortgage, tax and utilities, then negotiate inspection requests.
  • Cash sale: the buyer accepts the home as it stands, you pick the closing date, and there are no financing delays.
  • Either way, the deed is filed at the county clerk, whose fee schedule appears in the County Clerk Manual.

Get the closing date and title-work costs spelled out on paper, then get a listing agent's estimate to compare.

What if the house is rented or belonged to someone who died?

Each one adds a step before you can hand over keys. A tenant must be removed through a notice to vacate and, if needed, a justice court case. A house left by will may need that will admitted in court, and the State Law Library gives a four year window from the date of death.

  • Tenant: written notice to vacate is usually at least three days unless the lease says otherwise.
  • Small estate: the affidavit route covers estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, and it needs court approval.
  • No court filing yet: an affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement, and buyers do not have to accept it.

Where nobody has opened an estate yet, see a Texas attorney before signing.

More questions about Missouri City, TX

How fast can a Missouri City house close for cash?

Often within a few weeks, because there is no lender underwriting. The real pace depends on title work, a Fort Bend or Harris County lien search, and whether you need extra time to move. Ask for a closing date in writing.

Which county do I deal with if my Missouri City home is near the county line?

Your address decides. Missouri City spans Fort Bend and Harris counties, so the appraisal district and tax office are Fort Bend's or Harris County's depending on the parcel. Look up your account number on your tax bill to see which one applies.

Is the Missouri City tax rate for fiscal 2027 adopted?

Yes. The city's September 22, 2026 press release says the council adopted $0.578363 per $100 of taxable value for fiscal 2027. That is the city's portion only and excludes county, school and district rates.

Do I owe taxes if I sell partway through the year?

The tax lien attaches on January 1, so the year's bill belongs to the property and gets settled at closing. The title company usually prorates it between buyer and seller. Check the settlement statement line by line.

Where can I find my Missouri City property's tax breakdown?

Start with the city's Tax Information page for the unit rates, then your county appraisal district for your parcel's value and exemptions. The Fort Bend tax office branch on Texas Parkway can answer billing questions by phone.

It incorporated on April 15, 1910, with 1,126 residents, and it grew as a shipping and distribution hub where U.S. highways 77 and 83 meet in northwestern Cameron County.

Vegetables and cotton carried the early economy. Wartime installations then lifted the population from 23,000 in 1950 to 41,000 in 1960, and Harlingen Air Force Base shut in 1962. Local leaders bought and reused the base and its housing, and the entry credits that move for a broader economy that now includes Valley International Airport and an industrial airpark where bombers once landed.

The same entry names Valley Baptist Medical Center as a major health care anchor, and lists the Marine Military Academy and Texas State Technical Institute among its schools. The Comptroller lists a school-district homestead exemption for anyone living in the house, with an extra layer for seniors and disabled owners. Most Texas lenders skip the courthouse and use the power of sale written into the deed of trust. Sales take place on a month's first Tuesday at a spot the commissioners court picks, which for Harlingen means Cameron County. Selling before that day lets you choose your buyer and date. Under a federal rule a lender normally waits until a loan is more than 120 days behind before it begins. That gives you a window to act, but it is a short one, so call your servicer early and ask about loss mitigation.

Ask the Cameron County Clerk in Brownsville. The appraisal district's site tells visitors to go to the clerk for deed copies and subdivision plats, since it keeps neither.

Its guides name three common proofs: an executor's deed after administration, a court order paired with the will (a muniment of title), and an affidavit of heirship placed in the public record. No judge reviews that affidavit, and nothing forces a buyer or title insurer to accept it, so learn early what the buyer's title company will take.

That midpoint covers owner-occupied Harlingen homes in the 2020 to 2024 survey. Your house depends on its condition, size and block, so get written offers or an appraisal.

What should a Kyle seller know about the town?

Kyle was laid out in 1880 when two landowners deeded 200 acres to the International-Great Northern Railroad for a townsite, and it drew families and businesses from the nearby settlements of Mountain City and Blanco. The state historical association's entry says the Balcones Escarpment meets the blackland prairie here, with farming to the east and ranching to the west.

The town incorporated in 1928. Growth came in waves: five residential subdivisions opened in 1984 and 1985, and three of them went bankrupt in the late 1980s slump. That boom and bust pattern is worth remembering when you read older deed restrictions or plat notes on a Kyle property.

Kyle is served by the Hays Consolidated Independent School District, which is a common first question from buyers. Check the attendance zone for your street with the district before listing.

How does the Hays County tax cycle affect a Kyle sale?

Taxes are billed once a year, and the lien for that year attaches on January 1, so a seller owes a share of the year's bill whenever the sale closes. The Hays County Tax Office says the certified roll arrives from the Hays Central Appraisal District, and the tax statements go out in October.

A bill still open on February 1 the next year is delinquent and starts to collect penalty and interest. The Planning Department offers free pre-development meetings by appointment on Thursday afternoons, aimed at people planning subdivisions or site work. The department says Texas has required a 30-day review timeline for new subdivisions since September 1, 2019. If you own a large tract on the edge of town and want to sell to a builder, expect the buyer to ask about zoning and plat status first.

What does the Kyle deed filing look like?

Recording happens at the Hays County Clerk's office, since Texas files deeds where the land lies. The clerk can accept the deed only once the signer's acknowledgment is taken by a notary, or two subscribing witnesses have sworn to it.

Texas lists a $5.00 charge for page one and $4.00 for later pages, with other clerk fees on top. Your title company normally files for you. Ask the Hays County Clerk for the current fee list if you plan a direct family transfer.

How quickly can a Pflugerville house be sold?

That depends on the route you take. A cash buyer may close within weeks, whereas a listing adds showings, an inspection and loan approval. Pflugerville is fifteen miles north of Austin on Farm Road 1825, and local buyers often measure it against Austin and nearby Round Rock.

Cash usually means a lower price in return for speed and a closing day of your choosing. A listing may net more but brings repairs, staging and a loan contingency. Compare both on paper.

What is Pflugerville's growth story?

Pflugerville lies on Farm Road 1825 in northeastern Travis County. The Texas State Historical Association traces the name to Henry Pfluger, who arrived from Germany with his family in 1849; residents opened a school in 1872 and a Lutheran church in 1875.

A post office opened in 1893 under postmaster Louis Bohls. Around the mid-1890s about 250 people lived here and used Round Rock, eight miles northwest, for banking and shipping. After the Missouri, Kansas and Texas line ran just outside town in 1904, the population doubled to 500 within a decade.

People drifted to Austin after World War II, and by 1949 only 380 remained. Growth resumed in the 1960s, around the time of incorporation, and between 1980 and 1988 no Texas community grew faster. For a seller, the lesson is that houses here came in waves of new subdivisions, so builder and age tell a buyer more than the street does.

What else shaped Pflugerville before the suburban boom?

The handbook describes a small town with a weekly newspaper, the Press, published from 1907 to 1942. In the early 1920s several nearby school districts merged into the Pflugerville high school, which made the town a school center for the surrounding farms. A later weekly, the Pflag, began in 1980, just as the boom started.

The town's German farming roots survive in its name. The Pfluger family arrived in 1849, but the handbook says no real community formed at the site until after the Civil War, so the settlement is younger than the name suggests.

For a seller, local history is mostly color, but it supports one practical point. Older farmhouses and early town lots near the old center are a different product from tract homes built in the 1980s and after, and buyers price them differently. Say plainly which kind of house you have.

What does a Texas tax bill mean for a Pflugerville seller?

No state property tax exists in Texas, so the bill comes from local units like the county, school district and city. Value is set as of January 1 by the appraisal district, and that same day the year's tax lien attaches.

Bills go out near October 1. Whatever is unpaid on February 1 is late and draws a six percent penalty and one percent interest, with a possible collection fee of up to 20 percent. Homestead value notices arrive near April 1, and protests are generally due May 15.

Your deed is recorded by the clerk of the county containing the land, here the Travis County Clerk, after you sign it before a notary.

The clerk manual sets $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for every further page, with extra records fees. Your closing statement will show the total, and a warranty deed is typical.

What if the Pflugerville house has foreclosure or estate problems?

Every one of these runs on a short clock. A default notice gives you 20 days to pay the arrears and reinstate, and the sale notice must follow at least 21 days ahead of a first-Tuesday auction.

A lender whose sale falls short has two years to sue for the gap, and any surplus goes to junior lienholders, then to you. For an inherited house, a will is normally probated within four years of death, and an estate up to $75,000 not counting the homestead may use a small estate affidavit.

  • Behind on payments: get the reinstatement figure in writing.
  • Back taxes: ask the collector about an installment plan.
  • Inherited house: settle who may sign before accepting an offer.

What should I gather before showing a Pflugerville house?

Buyers in a fast-built suburb ask the same questions again and again, so answer them before they do. Start with the paperwork that proves what the house is and what has been done to it.

  • Permits and receipts for additions, roofs, air conditioning and fences.
  • The most recent tax bill and appraisal notice, plus any owners' association dues and rules.
  • Utility bills for a typical summer and winter month, since buyers from Austin will ask.

Then walk the property as an inspector would. Check the roof, the foundation line, the garage door, drainage around the slab and the water heater. Small foundation cracks and doors that stick draw attention, and a repair estimate in hand is better than a surprise at the inspection.

If you would rather not do any of that, a direct buyer will usually take it in present condition. Just make sure the written offer says so and that no repair requests can be added later without your agreement.

How should I compare offers on a Pflugerville house?

Judge each offer by what reaches your account and when. Deduct commissions, repairs, carrying costs, concessions and title charges from each price, then compare.

Ask if the buyer will close on your date, whether an inspection can end the deal, who buys the title policy and whether earnest money is required. If an owners' association covers the street, request its status letter early.

Travis County, since the handbook places Pflugerville in northeastern Travis County. Ask the title company to confirm your parcel's county before the deed is drafted.

In the 1980s. The Handbook of Texas calls it the fastest-growing community in the state from 1980 through 1988, and its population reached 16,335 by 2000.

After January 31. Interest and penalty start on February 1 under the Comptroller's calendar, and the penalty keeps rising monthly until July 1.

Usually May 15, unless the notice arrives late and 30 days from delivery is later. Because the value dates from January 1, it also feeds into the year's tax split at closing.

Where is Rowlett located and how do the lake and county line shape a sale?

Rowlett is a lakeside city of about 22 square miles in the Dallas area, mostly in Dallas County with a western edge of Rockwall County. Dalrock Road is the county dividing line, so the county that handles your taxes depends on which side of that road your house sits on.

The city says Lake Ray Hubbard, a water reservoir and recreational lake, surrounds it on two sides. The area was first settled in the 1840s, a post office opened in 1880 under the name Morris, and the name changed to Rowlett after Rowlett Creek. The Greenville and Dallas Railroad arrived in 1889, and the Bankhead Highway reached town in 1921. Rowlett incorporated in 1952 by a vote of 84 citizens.

The city says the lake's completion in 1971 made Rowlett a lakefront community, and that population grew from 5,100 in 1978 to about 64,000. Water on two sides shapes buyer interest, and a shoreline house may raise different insurance and survey questions than one inland.

How can you sell a Rowlett house in a hurry?

Three paths cover most situations: an agent listing, a direct sale to an investor, or a sale to someone who plans repairs. Weigh how soon you need money against how much work the house needs.

  • A listing suits a house in showing condition when you can wait on lender approval and appraisal.
  • A direct investor sale fits a house with deferred work, a rental history or a tenant who cannot leave quickly.
  • A renovator sale is for homes with code issues or dated systems.

Collect two written offers and learn who pays closing costs. A house that has been rented needs the registration check in the next section.

Does Rowlett regulate rental houses, and does that affect a sale?

Yes. Rowlett requires annual registration of single-family houses and duplexes used as rentals, and inspections apply when tenants change. This matters for a former rental, since a buyer may ask whether it is registered and current.

  • Annual registration is $50.00 per property.
  • An inspection is required at each tenant change, and the new tenant cannot move in until it passes. The inspection fee is $75.00.
  • If a tenant moves in before approval, the owner is charged $200.00.
  • The water utility account must be current, and a floor plan is required with the application.

Short-term rentals are tighter. Rowlett adopted its short-term rental ordinance in April 2025, and the registration page lists a $2,000 annual application fee with permits expiring January 31. A 1,000-foot separation requirement began in August 2026 for short-term rentals, applications are first-come, and owners must file hotel occupancy tax quarterly, including zero filings. The page says platforms like Airbnb and VRBO do not collect or remit that tax for Rowlett.

An owner running a short-term rental should tell buyers about the permit status, because the permit is tied to the owner and the property.

  • A designated local contact who is reachable 24 hours a day.

  • A site plan, floor plan, parking plan and emergency evacuation plan.
  • A guest safety sheet displayed inside, and signage on the exterior near the front door.
  • A city inspection approved before anyone occupies the property, with short-term rentals inspected quarterly through the MyGov portal.

The city also created a 1,000-foot rule on August 4, 2026 that bars renting to a registered sex offender within 1,000 feet of places where children commonly gather, and it applies to both short and long-term rentals. Complaints about a short-term rental can be made by phone or online through the platform the city names.

How are Rowlett property taxes split between two counties?

Because Rowlett lies in Dallas and Rockwall Counties, a house is appraised by Dallas Central Appraisal District or Rockwall Central Appraisal District, depending on its location. Check your tax statement to see which district and which county tax office applies.

Dallas CAD allows a homeowner who moves away temporarily to keep the exemption if no other principal residence is set up and a return is planned within two years, with longer allowed for military service abroad or a care facility stay.

Dallas CAD also explains a tax deferral for owners who qualify by age or disability: payment of taxes is postponed while you own and live in the home, but it is not cancelled, and five percent interest accrues each year. When the property is sold or transferred to an estate or heirs, the taxes and interest become due. That is the item to raise with a title company, since it will be paid from proceeds.

Which dates on the Texas tax calendar matter when you sell in Rowlett?

Texas sets one calendar for every city, and it applies here: appraisals are as of January 1, bills go out around October 1, and tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent.

What does Dallas CAD require when a new owner applies for a homestead exemption?

The applicant has to own and occupy the home on the January 1 of the application year, and Dallas CAD asks for a copy of a Texas driver's license or ID whose address matches the homestead address. That is useful to tell a buyer, because the ID address change must be done at a state driver license office after closing.

  • A single or married owner may be able to apply online.
  • Each individual owner who lives there, apart from married couples, completes a separate application, and exemption is split by percent of ownership.
  • Any rented or non-homestead part of the property, such as a room over a garage, must be listed by square footage.
  • For a house inherited without a recorded deed in the heir's name, the heir supplies an affidavit, the owner's death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation.

Dallas CAD says that filing a homestead application is free, and it warns that false statements or claiming homestead on more than one property is a crime under the Penal Code.

Do you need a permit in Rowlett before listing?

A permit is not needed for a sale, but past work should have been permitted. Rowlett runs an online permitting system through which permit applications and contractor registrations are submitted. Ask the city's building safety staff if you are unsure about work done on your house.

What if the house is in foreclosure or inherited?

In either case, call a title company early. A lender's foreclosure sale is set for a first Tuesday after a notice period, and an estate needs the right deed or court order recorded with the clerk of the county that holds the land lies, either Dallas or Rockwall.

Whichever county holds the land. Most of Rowlett is in Dallas County and a western part is in Rockwall County, with Dalrock Road as the dividing line, so check your tax statement.

Rowlett requires annual registration of rental single-family houses and duplexes, at $50.00 per property. If the house is currently rented, ask the city whether registration is current before you list.

Ask the city. Rowlett's page lists an annual application, a January 31 expiration and a 1,000-foot separation rule, but it does not say a permit follows the sale.

Yes, if you qualify for the deferral that Dallas CAD describes for older or disabled owners. The postponed tax plus five percent annual interest comes due when the home is sold.

How do I sell a Victoria, TX house on a short timeline?

Victoria serves as the commercial focus of the counties around it, so interest can come from town and from the surrounding ranch and farm country. Before you pick a route, find your loan payoff and the amount of any unpaid property tax.

Where is Victoria and how did it begin?

Victoria is the Victoria County seat, at the meeting of U.S. highways 59, 77 and 87, and the Handbook of Texas calls it the largest city in the central coastal region. It stands on the Guadalupe River at a site once called Cypress Grove.

Martin De Leon founded the settlement in 1824 as Guadalupe Victoria, after the first president of Mexico, and it was incorporated under the Republic of Texas in 1839. It grew as a stop on the La Bahia Road and a junction linking Lavaca Bay ports, San Antonio, Austin and northern Mexico. Rail came in 1861, with more lines in the 1870s and 1880s.

The City of Roses nickname goes back to an editor of the Victoria Advocate in the 1880s. The paper first appeared in 1846 and is described as the state's second oldest existing newspaper. De Leon Plaza still anchors the historic downtown.

What kept Victoria growing?

Oil, manufacturing, agribusiness, petrochemicals, tourism and outdoor recreation produced the area's income, per the Handbook of Texas, and the city serves as a medical center for a multi-county area. Foster Army Air Field operated until 1957 and then became the municipal airport.

The population rose from 16,126 in 1950 to 33,047 in 1960 and 55,076 in 1980, then reached 60,603 in 2000. With that much postwar growth, plenty of Victoria housing is decades old, so write down when the roof, plumbing and wiring were last updated.
