How do Coppell schools figure into a sale?

Coppell Independent School District anchors the city's family market. The district describes eighteen campuses and more than 13,000 students in grades PreK-12: eleven elementary schools, three middle schools, two high schools, a ninth grade campus and an alternative campus.

The district says it employs over 1,500 people, making it one of the largest employers in town, and that 92 percent of graduates go on to university study. It also reports 37 National Merit Semifinalists in 2015. School quality is a headline for many families, so name the district in your listing materials. Leave attendance zones to the district, since boundaries can change.

Why does the January 1 date matter for Coppell property tax?

Each parcel gets its value on January 1, and that same day the year's tax lien attaches. Selling in March or September leaves the lien in place; the settlement statement splits the year's bill between the parties.

Because Coppell spans Dallas County and Denton County, your own bill names the appraisal district and collector for your parcel. Mailing starts about October 1. Payment is expected by January 31, and from February 1 late charges build.

  • April 30: common cutoff for many exemption applications.
  • The later of May 15 or 30 days after the appraisal notice arrives: usual protest deadline.
  • June 30 of the next year: second installment if you split payment.

Dates come from the Comptroller's deadline calendar and payment guidance.

What homestead protections should a Coppell owner confirm before listing?

Confirm that your homestead exemption is on file. The Comptroller says school districts must grant $140,000 on a residence homestead, with $60,000 more for older or disabled owners.

Yearly appraisal growth on a homestead is capped at 10 percent, starting the year after the exemption first applies. A purchaser closing after January 1 can often claim the exemption right away if the seller never had it. If your account lacks an exemption you qualify for, ask the appraisal district about filing before the listing goes live, because the tax figure shows up in buyers' payment estimates.

Read the Comptroller's exemptions page and its limits page.

What does the deed filing involve for a Coppell sale?

Once the sale closes, the title company sends the deed to the Dallas or Denton County clerk, whichever covers the parcel. A notary seal or two witnesses must back the signature.

A courts manual prints $5.00 for the first page of a deed and $4.00 per added page, plus records fees. Charges change, so request the live schedule. Omitting the grantee's mailing address can add cost.

  • Put the buyer's mailing address on the deed.
  • Ask for a file-stamped copy once indexed.
  • Keep the settlement statement with your tax papers.

Source: county clerk manual.

What if the Coppell house carries a mortgage default, an heir's claim or a tenant?

Each case runs on its own clock. With a defaulted loan the borrower gets 20 days after the default notice to catch up, and the auction notice precedes the sale by at least three weeks.

Inherited houses move through a court order or sworn affidavit, depending on the facts. A rental starts with written notice to the tenant before any justice court case. Cash buyers will sometimes take a house with these matters open, but speak with a Texas attorney and the title company first.

Sources: State Law Library pages on foreclosure, probate and eviction.

How has Coppell's housing stock changed over time?

The Handbook describes Coppell in 1990 as primarily upper-middle-class homeowners, with a population of 16,881, and says the population passed 35,000 by 2000. Rapid building through those decades means a good share of Coppell houses likely date from the late twentieth century, so roofs, HVAC units and water heaters may be reaching replacement age.

Before you list, walk through the house as an inspector would. Note the age of the roof, the condition of the foundation and fences, and any past repairs. A buyer financing through a lender will have an appraisal and inspection, while a cash buyer will build repair costs into the price. Either way, a short written list of upgrades, with dates and receipts, shortens the back and forth.

  • Roof, HVAC and water heater: age and last service.
  • Foundation or drainage repairs, with invoices.
  • Permits for additions or finished garages.
  • HOA documents, if the neighborhood has an association.

Both. The city crosses the county line, and the parcel's spot decides your appraisal district and recording office. The tax bill shows which.

When are Coppell tax bills due?

Most bills are due by January 31. A split-payment option puts half at November 30 and half at June 30 of the next year.

Can I protest my appraisal if I plan to sell?

Yes, filing by the later of May 15 or 30 days after the notice arrives. A lower value also helps the next owner's bill.

Does a cash sale change what I owe in taxes?

No. Liens and taxes work the same in any sale, and they come out of your proceeds at closing. Get a payoff statement in writing before you agree.

Usually the title company. Afterward you can request a stamped copy from the clerk.

Can I sell my Friendswood house fast for cash?

Yes. Friendswood owners can accept a cash offer, list through an agent, or ask a buyer to close after the move. Cash fits a house needing work, a tight deadline or a title problem.

Friendswood is a residential community south of Houston, and the state history calls it a bedroom suburb of the space-industry and Houston job centers. A tidy house may do well on the open market, while a damaged house or one tied up in an estate is the kind investors quote quickly.

  • Ask each buyer how long the offer is valid and what could change it after their inspection.
  • Ask who covers title insurance, recording and any association transfer fees.
  • Have the buyer name the title company and put a target date in writing.

Because the state history says four creeks, Clear Creek among them, drain the land, it is worth asking your insurer and the county about drainage history for your lot, then telling buyers what you learn. Compare offers by the amount you receive after payoff, taxes and fees. That figure matters more than the headline price, especially when one buyer asks you to make repairs and another does not. Ask each buyer to show how they reached the number, including any deduction for repairs.

How did Friendswood begin, and what is it now?

Friendswood is an incorporated residential community on Farm Road 518, about twenty miles south of Houston and twenty-seven miles northwest of Galveston, in northwestern Galveston and southern Harris counties, according to the Texas State Historical Association.

English Quakers who first settled in Crosby County bought more than 1,500 acres from J. C. League in 1895 and named the settlement in honor of the Friends. The land was drained by four creeks: Chigger, Coward's, Mary's and Clear. A post office opened in 1899, and early residents grew Satsuma oranges, strawberries, figs and rice. Oil turned up in the 1930s.

Change came with the space program. After the NASA Manned Spacecraft Center opened about ten miles away in 1962, many residents began commuting there or to Houston, and Friendswood became a bedroom suburb. The community incorporated in 1960. The same source records growth from 1,675 people in 1968 to 13,585 in 1980 and 22,814 in 1990. Friendswood Academy, built from pine felled by the 1900 Galveston hurricane, graduated its first class in 1907 and served as the local church.

Does Friendswood sit in one county or two?

The city lies in both Galveston and Harris counties, which means taxes and records can change with the side of the county line your parcel falls on. Your tax bill and your deed will name the county. Start there before you call any office.

The Galveston Central Appraisal District lists the City of Friendswood and Friendswood ISD among the taxing units it serves, and it shows Friendswood ISD as having its own tax assessor-collector, separate from the one that serves the city. You can see this on its taxing units page. That means a Galveston County parcel in the city may have bills from more than one collector, so every payoff should be gathered before closing.

For a parcel in the Harris County part of the city, the appraisal district for Harris County handles values. Ask that office, not the Galveston one, if your lot is on the north side.

What shaped Seguin and its housing stock?

Seguin was laid out in 1838 as Walnut Springs and renamed in February 1839. It was incorporated on February 7, 1853, according to the Handbook of Texas, and it already had a school chartered in 1849. The Handbook says that schoolhouse was recognized by the state in 1962 as the oldest continuously used school building in Texas.

Older parts of town therefore include homes with a long history, and the Handbook mentions antebellum houses including the Sebastopol House State Historic Structure. Houses of that age tend to need roof, wiring or plumbing work, which a buyer will price in.

The local economy started in agriculture and trade, took a lift when oil was found in the Darst Creek fields in the late 1920s, and later added manufacturing and services. Texas Lutheran University, which moved to a farm near Seguin in 1912, adds a campus to the mix.

Seguin's first economy was farming and trade. Oil from the Darst Creek fields, fifteen miles east, lifted the town in the late 1920s.

The city changed from a mayor-council to a council-manager form of government in 1986. Attractions include Max Starcke Park, the Guadalupe County Coliseum and fairgrounds, where the Texas State High School Rodeo has run since 1984.

Education runs through town too. A homestead appraisal cannot rise more than 10 percent a year, starting the year after the owner first qualifies. Owners 65 or older or disabled also get a school tax ceiling fixed at the amount paid in the year they qualified.

A tenant can stay through a sale. Getting the house vacant means written notice and a justice court filing, which a sale with the tenant in place skips.

How is Weatherford laid out, and which roads matter to buyers?

Weatherford sits where U.S. Highways 180 and 80 meet, with Interstate 20 along the southern edge of the city. Farm roads 920, 2421, 51 and 1884 and State Highway 171 also serve it, according to the Texas State Historical Association.

The city stands on the crest of a divide between the Trinity and Brazos valleys. Sellers should note that a house is judged partly by how quickly its owner can reach I-20 toward Fort Worth. Say so in your listing description, since commute time is among the first things a buyer asks about.

Weatherford's First Monday Fair began as a trade day when court was in session and farmers brought produce and livestock to town. It now features a flea market, produce and livestock, and the crowds it draws can help a nearby seller who schedules an open house that weekend.

Weatherford Lake lies just outside the city limits and is a popular recreation spot, which gives houses on that side of town a lifestyle angle. Weatherford College, which has operated since the 1890s, also draws renters and staff, so a small rental house near it may find a tenant or an investor buyer.

Parker County voters picked this site for the county seat in an election, and the town took its name from a state senator who co-wrote the bill creating the county. It was incorporated in 1858 and received a post office in 1859. For its first decade it was the principal frontier settlement in North Texas.

Rail arrived with the Texas and Pacific Railway in 1880, the Santa Fe line seven years later and a local line in 1891. Those connections made the town a shipping point for farmers and ranchers, and agribusiness stayed central through the twentieth century. Watermelon became the main local crop after 1900, and the First Monday Fair, held on the first Monday of each month, still carries on the old trade-day custom.

Population figures show the scale of recent growth. Weatherford had an estimated 5,000 residents in the mid 1890s, just over 6,000 in 1920, over 8,000 in 1950, 14,804 in 1990 and about 19,000 in 2000. In the 1890s it already had seven churches, three banks and four hotels. Oilfield equipment, rubber and plastic plants joined the economy in later decades, and over 400 businesses operated in the city by 1990.

The town also sat midway on the stage run between Fort Worth and Fort Belknap, and for its first twenty-five years it served as a refuge for county residents during the Indian raids that lasted into the early 1870s. Those layers of history explain why the street grid and housing stock vary so much from block to block.

Homes near the downtown core and along the older rail corridors predate the postwar growth. Expect buyers and inspectors to look closely at foundations, drainage and original utilities in those houses, and plan repairs or pricing around what they find.

The city says Copperas Cove began in the 1870s as a rural ranching and farming community, and two events lifted its economy: the railroad arriving in the late 1880s and the building of Camp Hood, later Fort Hood, in 1942. The name comes from a spring with mineral-tasting water.

The same guide says a hearing is set within a few weeks of filing, a tenant may appeal to county court within five days of judgment, and a writ of possession follows only after the final judgment, with a day's notice before removal. How did Cleburne grow around the railroads?

Cleburne began as a railroad and wagon-road town, and that background explains much of what makes it different from newer Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs. The Handbook of Texas places the city on U.S. Highway 67, thirty miles south of Fort Worth. The site sat near the earliest county road and had a good water source on West Buffalo Creek. It became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867, when a central county seat was needed to replace Buchanan, and the town was named for a Confederate general. It incorporated in May 1871.

Rail made the town. A railroad line from Fort Worth through Cleburne to Temple opened in 1881, and in 1898 and 1899 the Santa Fe built its central machine shops here, which helped double the population in the 1890s. The population was 683 in 1870, 3,727 in 1890, 12,820 in 1920, and 26,005 in 2000. The same entry names Lake Pat Cleburne, the Layland Museum in the old Carnegie Library building, and the Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Station nearby as a major employer.

Transport kept layering on. A spur to Egan opened in 1902, the "Boll Weevil" line ran from 1904 to 1924, an interurban from Fort Worth served the city from 1912, and a local streetcar ran from 1911 to 1917. A Carnegie Library opened in 1904 and a junior college operated here from 1909 to 1919. In the 1920s all four city banks failed and a 1922 Santa Fe strike deepened the slump, and the population was 10,558 by 1940. A Civilian Conservation Corps camp built Cleburne State Recreation Park, which opened in 1941.

After 1945 nearness to the Dallas-Fort Worth region brought steady growth: 22,205 residents by 1990 and 26,005 in 2000. The Handbook also names Lake Pat Cleburne, the Layland Museum in the old Carnegie Library building, and the Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Station nearby as a major employer.

Where do I go for Cleburne property tax values?

Johnson County values come from the Central Appraisal District of Johnson County at 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne. The posted hours are 8:00am to 4:30pm on weekdays, with a drop box in the front door, and the phone is (817) 648-3000. Exemption questions go to exemptions@johnsoncad.org.

The district posted that certified 2026 appraisal data became available for download on August 10, 2026. It also reported a 2026 software upgrade with a period of dual data entry, so confirm any exemption on your account with the office itself instead of trusting a screen.

The statewide calendar behind a Johnson County bill: valuation and the tax lien date fall on January 1, homestead notices of value go out around April 1, and the protest deadline is May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later. Texas lenders with a power of sale in the deed of trust can foreclose at a courthouse auction without suing, which for a Cleburne house means Johnson County. The borrower has 20 days from receiving the default notice to catch up.

The sale notice must reach the borrower at least 21 days ahead and also be posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk. If the lender sues afterward over a shortfall, the suit must come within two years. Selling before the auction may protect your equity, so act early if a notice has arrived.

  • Tenant: 3 days of written notice, a justice court filing, then a 6-day wait after judgment before a writ of possession; an appeal to county court is due within 5 days.

Hurst grew late and fast. Farmers settled the area in the 1840s, and the Rock Island railroad arrived in 1903. The stop was first called Ormel, with a post office from 1904 to 1909, before the name Hurst was adopted in 1909, the Handbook of Texas records.

The real change came in 1951, when Bell Aircraft announced a helicopter plant and residents voted 36 to 24 to incorporate, partly to keep Fort Worth from annexing the town. Tarrant County College opened a northeast campus in 1968, North East Mall followed in 1972, and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport opened in January 1974. By 1970 the population was more than 27,200 and the Handbook estimates about 40,000 in 2020.

That postwar boom explains why so many Hurst houses are fifty to seventy years old. Older houses can carry original wiring, plumbing and slab issues, which buyers will price in.

Employment shaped Hurst's streets as much as the railroad did. The Handbook of Texas says the Bell Helicopter workforce topped 11,000 at the height of the Vietnam War, with many workers building Huey helicopters. In 1958, with 8,500 residents, about half of working Hurst residents commuted to Dallas and about 40 percent to Fort Worth.

Retail followed jobs. North East Mall opened in 1972 and doubled Hurst's retail sales in a month, and it was still the largest mall in Tarrant County in the early 1990s. The Handbook also says Hurst was blocked from growing south by Fort Worth, pursued annexations in other directions from 1956 to 1958, and by the 1970s had nearly reached its limits.

Federal rules usually hold a servicer back until a home loan is well past four months behind. A sale that closes first can protect equity and credit, so compare it with the other options and speak with a housing counselor or attorney.

Hurst deeds are filed with the Tarrant County clerk, who can quote the records charges for your instrument.

What does Texas allow when a Hurst house has unwelcome occupants or a tenant?

Texas treats tenants and squatters differently. A tenant gets written notice to vacate, and the landlord goes to justice court if the tenant stays. A person who entered with no right at all can be handled through Property Code chapter 24B, which lets an owner ask the sheriff or constable for removal, unless the occupant is family or a past or present tenant or a suit is pending.

Registration must be renewed every year by December 31, and a certificate must be renewed after two years, when tenants change, or when ownership changes during the registration year. With back taxes owed, the Comptroller says some collectors allow payment plans of up to 36 months, and a homestead owner can require one. Ask the Dallas County tax office what your account shows.

What if the house was inherited or I am behind on the mortgage?

Both situations carry deadlines in Texas, and a sale can still work. Four years is the window to probate a will, and a small estate affidavit, muniment of title or affidavit of heirship may fit depending on the facts. A title company decides what it will accept.

The State Law Library also says a federal rule generally bars a lender from starting foreclosure on most home loans until the loan is more than 120 days delinquent, and that lenders face a two-year window for a deficiency suit. The application asks for a driver's license copy, the passed inspection report, a floor plan with room dimensions and a signed Chapter 26 acknowledgement. A building with three or more units needs a multi-family permit that expires each December 31, at $13 per dwelling unit, with an inspection fee of $150 per unit or building in violation.

If a buyer wants to keep operating the rental, ask Code Enforcement whether the permit transfers or must be reissued. For a tenant in place, a written notice to vacate of three days or more is the usual starting point when the lease is silent, and any eviction suit is filed in justice court.

What Texas rules apply if I fall behind on the mortgage in Farmers Branch?

Texas uses non-judicial foreclosure in most home loans, which moves faster than a court case. A borrower can usually catch up on the missed payments inside a 20-day window after the default notice, and the sale notice has to go out three weeks or more ahead of the auction.

Sales run on a first-Tuesday schedule in daytime hours, and the notice goes up at the courthouse and into the county clerk's records. After a sale, a deficiency suit must be filed within two years, and surplus funds go first to junior liens, then to the former owner.

Selling before the auction date can end the debt on your terms. Ask the lender for a written payoff and request a closing date that beats the posted sale.

What tax and filing steps does a Farmers Branch sale involve?

No state property tax exists in Texas; local units set the rates. Appraisal districts set value from the January 1 status of each parcel, notices for homesteads go out around April 1, and most protests are due by mid-May, or a month after the notice arrives if that date is later.

Bills arrive in October and turn delinquent once January 31 passes. The January 1 lien follows the land, so the title company normally divides the current year's tax between seller and buyer. The county tax office can give you the exact figure for your parcel, and the city can give its rate.

Deeds are filed at the clerk's office for the county holding the house, and the fee schedule there sets the cost.

What paperwork should I gather before I list in Farmers Branch?

A clean file speeds up every kind of buyer. Start with the recorded deed, your last tax statement, the mortgage payoff letter and the survey. Add receipts for roof, HVAC, plumbing and electrical work, plus any city permit records for additions.

For a house that was rented out, add the current lease, the rental license number if you hold one, the deposit amount and the rent roll. An owner-occupant buyer will want the tenant gone by closing, and a landlord buyer will want the lease assigned, so say which you prefer in the contract.

  • Deed, survey and tax statement.
  • Payoff letter and lender contact.
  • Permit records and repair receipts.
  • Lease, deposit and rent history for a tenant-occupied home.

Send copies to the title company early so a lien or name mismatch shows up well ahead of closing day. A seller who has a rental license should also ask the city what happens to it when the owner changes.

What can I say about Farmers Branch in a listing?

Commute time often comes up first, and workers here average 21.6 minutes to get to work by Census count. Census data also gives a bachelor's-or-higher share of 52.8 percent and a poverty rate of 11.4 percent. Retail sales of $1,694,624 thousand in 2022 point to a commercial base bigger than a bedroom suburb.

When you write a seller's description, stick to checkable facts: year built, roof age, last HVAC service and utility costs. The city's Community Services department can tell you about code history on a specific address.

More questions about Farmers Branch, TX

Is Farmers Branch easy to sell in quickly?

It can be, since buyers have plenty of nearby comparisons. Your own house prices on its condition, not on the $364,600 Census median.

Is a certificate of occupancy part of a Farmers Branch sale?

Ask Code Enforcement. The city's permit page lists a certificate of occupancy as a commercial requirement, and any rule for a residential change of ownership should be confirmed with the city prior to listing.

Can I run an estate sale before I sell my Farmers Branch home?

Yes, with registration. City code allows two garage-type sales a year, each up to three consecutive days, and estate sales are included in that rule.

What does an STR permit cost in Farmers Branch?

The city lists $120 per year and requires a passed inspection first. Applications run through a vendor called Host Compliance.

How long does a Texas foreclosure take once a notice is sent?

Borrowers get a 20-day cure window after the default notice, and the auction cannot come sooner than 21 days after the sale notice. The sale itself happens on a Tuesday early in the month.

What is it like to sell a house in La Porte, TX?

Selling in La Porte means dealing with a mature, industry-linked Gulf Coast city in Harris County, where flood risk and insurance questions come up in almost every buyer conversation. A house with clear flood history, current permits and an organized paper file sells faster.

The city's own history page says La Porte was incorporated on August 10, 1892, making it the oldest incorporated town in east Harris County. It began as a land venture by Colorado developers, became known for Sylvan Beach Park, and turned into what the city calls a bedroom community for industry after World War II, NASA and the Bayport Channel.

How did La Porte grow into the city it is today?

Developers laid out the town in 1891 and 1892 and promoted it to buyers in the Midwest and Northeast with special excursion trains. Citrus did not survive the freezes and the heavy gumbo soil, so the town leaned on figs, hay and the resort trade at Sylvan Beach.

A fire in June 1915 destroyed three blocks of Main Street, and a hurricane followed that July. Industry then reshaped the town: a chemical plant opened in 1945, and the city credits the Bayport Channel and the Barbours Cut terminal with later growth. The town of Lomax consolidated with La Porte in 1980, and Bayshore Municipal Utility District was annexed in 1987.

Those layers explain why La Porte has older bayside cottages, mid-century subdivisions and newer homes within a few miles of each other.

How does flood risk affect a La Porte home sale?

It affects price, insurance and buyer questions. La Porte says all properties in the city are susceptible to flooding, and names Galveston Bay, Little Cedar Bayou, Clear Creek and Armand Bayou among its main water sources across roughly 20 square miles.

The city lists past events that buyers will recall: Tropical Storm Allison in 2001, Hurricane Ike in 2008, two floods in 2015 and Hurricane Harvey in 2017. Buyers and lenders often ask which FEMA zone the house is in, so check it before you list.

  • Call the city engineer or use the city's GIS map to see your parcel's flood zone.
  • Gather any elevation certificate, past claim records and repair receipts.
  • Know that a new flood policy has a 30-day waiting period, as the city notes.
  • Remember that La Porte requires new and substantially improved structures to sit at least 12 inches above base flood elevation.

Why does Sylvan Beach still come up in La Porte conversations?

Sylvan Beach Park was the center of the town's early economy. The city says the land became a city park in 1893, was renamed Sylvan Beach in 1898, and the Moonlight Excursion train from Houston began running in the summer of 1900.

The resort faded after World War II and a series of hurricanes. The city's financial report notes the Sylvan Beach pier was badly damaged by Hurricane Ike in 2008 and has since been rebuilt, so waterfront buyers will ask about storm history and insurance.

For sellers inland, the story is different: the city says shipyards, chemical plants and the Bayport Channel turned La Porte into a bedroom community for industry. Collect repair receipts for roof, windows and drainage, which are the first things an inspector checks.

If you own an older home near the ship channel or the bay, ask the city engineer which FEMA map applied when the house was built. The city explains this historical map can matter in a dispute with a lender or insurance agent.

Do I need a permit to repair a La Porte house before selling?

Yes, if you work in the floodplain or do substantial repairs. The city says development in the floodplain without a permit is illegal, and that includes new construction, filling, grading and paving.

A structure is treated as new construction when repair or improvement cost equals or exceeds 50 percent of its market value. That rule can affect a buyer who plans a big renovation on a damaged house. Call the Planning and Development Department before you start work, and keep permit records for the buyer.

How are taxes split between buyer and seller in La Porte?

They are usually prorated at closing based on estimated taxes, and the real bill is worked out later in the year. The appraisal district points out that this does not change actual liability, so the final amount can differ from the estimate.

If the house has only a general homestead exemption, it normally stays for the whole tax year, and the buyer files a new application for the next year. If the seller is 65 or older or disabled and claims a new homestead elsewhere during the same year, the exemption on the sold house is prorated, which can raise that year's bill.

How does a La Porte deed reach the county records?

Harris County holds the records for La Porte land. Texas only lets a conveyance be recorded once it carries a notary's acknowledgment or two subscribing witnesses' oath, so schedule the signing with a notary present.

Your title company files the deed after closing.

  • List with an agent and price for the bay-area buyer pool, with repairs completed.
  • Sell as-is to a cash buyer when flood damage, deferred work or a deadline makes listing difficult.
  • Sell to a neighbor or relative with a written contract and title company closing.
  • Rent first if the house needs time, though that adds landlord duties.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What papers help a La Porte sale close smoothly?

Collect the deed, payoff letters, the latest Harris County tax statement, flood zone documents and any elevation certificate. Add receipts and permits for work done after storms, since La Porte's floodplain rules make permit history matter.

If the home sat in a flood event, note the claim dates and the repairs done. Buyers and lenders ask for them, and clear answers help your price hold.

  • Insurance declarations pages, including any flood policy.
  • Permit records from the Planning and Development Department.
  • Homestead exemption status and any over-65 ceiling on file.

More questions about La Porte, TX

Is flood insurance needed to sell a house in La Porte?

It is not required to sell, but buyers and lenders often ask for it. The city says basic homeowner's insurance does not cover flood and a new flood policy has a 30-day wait before it takes effect.

Who collects property tax on a La Porte house?

The Harris County Tax Office collects it, and the Harris Central Appraisal District sets value and handles exemptions. Taxes are due when billed and usually become delinquent on February 1 of the next year.

Can I sell a La Porte house that has flood damage?

Yes, you can sell it as-is or after repairs. If repair cost reaches 50 percent of the building's market value, the city treats it like new construction and requires permits and an elevation certificate.

When is the La Porte homestead filing window?

Regular applications are due between January 1 and April 30. Late applications are accepted for a general exemption up to two years after taxes became delinquent.

Do buyers pay La Porte taxes after closing?

Yes, the buyer owns the bill from closing forward, with the year's taxes prorated at closing on estimated figures. The final bill is calculated by the tax office later in the year.

What are the quick ways to sell a house in San Juan?

San Juan owners generally weigh three paths: an agent listing, a sale on their own, or a cash offer for the house in its current state. Cash is the shortest route, and a listing tends to bring the highest price for a house in good shape.

San Juan lies in south central Hidalgo County on Farm Road 1426 and State Highway Spur 374, about six miles northeast of McAllen, according to the Texas State Historical Association. Its school district name, Pharr-San Juan-Alamo, shows how closely the three towns are linked.

Before you accept any offer, ask what it assumes about repairs, who pays recording and title costs, and the closing date. A written answer to each lets you compare offers on equal terms.

What is San Juan's history, and how does it affect housing?

San Juan was organized in 1909 and reportedly named for John Closner. The city incorporated on December 29, 1917. The townsite lies on land from two Spanish grants made in 1767, and the Handbook says the first school building went up in 1918.

The economy grew from irrigated farming, with a cotton compress, a cannery and a cotton gin built in 1924. By 1945 the town had the largest plant in the South making concrete pipe for irrigation drainage, plus citrus and vegetable packing houses. The Virgen de San Juan del Valle Shrine, built in 1954, draws pilgrims and tourists, and a new shrine was dedicated in April 1980.

The Handbook records growth from 4,371 people in 1960 to 10,815 in 1992 and 26,229 in 2000. That fast growth means many houses are fairly recent, so keep receipts and records for repairs you have made.

Which school district and appraisal district cover a San Juan house?

The Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District, established on March 24, 1919, took in all of the schools in San Juan, according to the Handbook. Check your tax bill to confirm the district listed for your parcel.

Its website offers property search, an online portal for filing exemptions and appeals, and a homestead portal for homestead and over 65 applications. The district said it is accepting applications for Appraisal Review Board auxiliary members for 2026 and 2027, and its customer service line is 956-381-8466.

  • Use the property search to see your value, owner and tax history.
  • Use the portal to file an exemption or an appeal.
  • Use the truth in taxation site to see proposed rates from each taxing unit.
  • Use the Comptroller's taxpayer pamphlet for the protest process.

Ask the county tax office for your bill and the exact rate for each unit. We do not state a rate here because each unit sets its own.

What does the Virgen de San Juan del Valle Shrine mean for the city?

The shrine, built in 1954, drew pilgrims and tourists almost at once. The Handbook adds that on October 23, 1970 a rented single engine plane struck it while more than 130 people were inside, causing about $1.5 million in damage, and that a mass effort rebuilt it. The new shrine was dedicated in April 1980.

By the mid 1960s San Juan reported ten churches, three schools, two hospitals, a library, a bank and a newspaper, and the Handbook calls its economy agriculture and commerce with visitors to the shrine also important. The city is also known as home of the Bougainvillea Trail of Texas.

For a seller this means visitor traffic and a stable local identity, but no guarantee of price. Describe your block, its distance to schools and the shrine, and any recent work in plain terms.

What do the city's planning and permit offices handle in San Juan?

The City of San Juan Planning Department manages land use, zoning, permits, subdivisions and rezoning. It is made up of Health, Building and Code Enforcement divisions that watch zoning, safety and health rules. The office is at 512 S. Nebraska Ave. and can be reached at 956-223-2220.

The city runs an interactive GIS map that shows zoning and city limits, and it helps you find out whether you need city permits or utilities. It also lets you check whether a location falls under Hidalgo County Precinct 1 or 2 for services outside city jurisdiction.

Owners near the edge of town should start there. Whether a parcel sits inside city limits changes who regulates a garage conversion, an addition or a fence. Ask the office whether a permit is on file for earlier work.

  • Planning and Zoning: 956-223-2220, 512 S. Nebraska Ave.
  • Divisions: Health, Building and Code Enforcement.
  • Maps: the GIS map shows zoning, city limits and county precinct.

How do Texas tax penalties work if you owe on a San Juan house?

Bills arrive in the fall, and the Comptroller says unpaid taxes are delinquent from February 1.

The table below lays out how the penalty builds up after that, as printed by the Comptroller.

Delinquent tax penalties in Texas (Texas Comptroller)
WhenPenalty or interest

Each month until July 1Penalty continues to rise one percent a month; interest is one percent a month

A written request to waive penalty and interest has to be filed before the 181st day after the delinquency date. Installment plans of up to 36 months exist at some collectors and are required only for a residence homestead.

How do deeds, probate and tenants work for a San Juan seller?

Deeds for San Juan land go to the Hidalgo County Clerk, and the signer must appear before a notary or other authorized officer.

For an inherited house, a will can be probated within four years of the death, and a muniment of title can pass title when the estate has no debts apart from liens on the land. Heirs often need a title company to tell them which document a buyer's lender will accept.

A tenant complicates timing. Removal needs written notice and a justice court case, while selling with the tenant in place skips that process and keeps rent coming until closing.

What if the house is in foreclosure or needs major work?

Foreclosure in Texas is usually nonjudicial and ends in a public auction. A sale before that date can protect your equity, and excess proceeds after an auction go to junior liens before the former owner.

A house that needs a new roof, drainage work or electrical repairs suits an as is buyer, who takes on the work. You give up some price in exchange for skipping contractors and repair requests.

More questions about San Juan, TX

What school district is San Juan in?

The Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District, which the Handbook of Texas says was established in 1919 and took in all of the schools in San Juan. Your tax bill confirms it for your parcel.

Who appraises property in San Juan?

The Hidalgo County Appraisal District. It offers a property search, an online portal for exemptions and appeals, and a customer service line at 956-381-8466. Property search, the online portal and the homestead portal let you check a value or apply for an exemption without a visit.

Does San Juan have a planning office I can call about permits?

Yes. The Planning and Zoning department handles permits, zoning and rezoning, and can be reached at 956-223-2220. Its GIS map helps you check city limits and zoning.

When do unpaid taxes become delinquent?

On February 1 for most bills, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest start. The penalty rises to 12 percent on July 1.

Can an unpaid tax bill stop a San Juan sale?

It does not have to. A tax lien attaches on January 1, so the unpaid amount is normally settled from your proceeds at closing. Ask the county tax office for a payoff figure and have your title company include it.

Is a cash sale the best way to leave a Greenville house quickly?

Often it is, since no lender's appraisal stands between you and the closing date. A regular listing can still work if the home is in good order, though you will prep it and sit through showings.

Greenville is the Hunt County seat, about sixty miles northeast of Dallas on Interstate 30, so buyers come from a smaller pool than in the inner suburbs. A house that sits on the market for months can pick up carrying costs: taxes, insurance, utilities and mowing. Weigh those against the lower price a cash buyer may offer.

  • Agent listing: suits an updated house and a flexible schedule.
  • Private sale: suits owners who can manage contracts and disclosures.
  • Cash offer: suits a vacant house, an estate property or one with deferred repairs.

What should sellers know about Greenville and Hunt County?

Greenville was established in 1846, the same year the legislature created Hunt County, and the town takes its name from a Texas general. The Texas State Historical Association says residents chose a 640-acre prairie site donated by a surveyor, and the city incorporated in 1852. The blackland soil around town made it a cotton market, and railroads arrived between 1880 and 1896.

The city has a record of firsts in public services. In 1891 its government began running an electricity plant, which the state history calls the first municipally owned utility system in Texas. Aircraft work took over after World War II: a wartime airfield called Majors Field later hosted overhaul and defense electronics operations, and the state history names the defense electronics firm there as the city's largest employer.

Roads shape the map. Interstate 30, U.S. highways 380, 69 and 67, and State highways 224, 66 and 34 all pass through, and three railroads cross town. The population was 23,960 in 2000 after peaking near 27,750 in 1990. Annual events include the Hunt County Fair in August and the Cotton Pickin' Arts and Crafts Jubilee in November.

Older homes close to the downtown square date from the era of the cotton boom and wartime expansion. Whatever the age of your house, a folder of receipts for roof, plumbing and electrical work gives a buyer something concrete to read.

How did Greenville's growth shape its neighborhoods?

Growth came in waves, and each wave left housing behind. The town counted about 3,000 people in 1884, roughly 5,000 by 1892 and 14,000 by 1914, helped by rail lines and a cotton trade that shipped over $1 million of cotton a year in the early 1890s. Streetcar service even reached a college campus in 1912.

Between 1933 and 1952 the population rose from 12,407 to 14,697, and during 1941 and 1942 the city issued $60,000 in bonds to buy and improve 760 acres for a wartime airfield. An aircraft overhaul company leased part of that field in 1951, started with 400 workers, and by the late 1960s a successor employed 4,600. Houses built for that workforce are now several decades old and may carry original wiring, plumbing and roofs.

If your property dates from one of those periods, say so in your listing or your conversation with a buyer, and ask Hunt CAD for the year-built on its record so your description matches.

What do Greenville property taxes look like for an owner?

The Hunt County Appraisal District, known as Hunt CAD, appraises all real and business personal property in the county, and the county tax assessor-collector sends the bill. The district's site offers online property search, a homestead exemption portal and a truth-in-taxation tool, and it warns owners not to pay anyone a fee to file a homestead application because the district charges nothing.

Texas has no state property tax. County, city and school district each set a rate for your house, while the appraisal district assigns the value as of the first of January. Bills mail around October 1. Per the Comptroller, a balance still open on February 1 becomes delinquent and starts drawing penalty and interest.

Hunt CAD's home page notes that requests such as property splits or combines made after April 1, 2026 apply to the 2027 tax year. That kind of cutoff is worth knowing if you are dividing a tract before a sale.

  • Protests are usually due May 15, unless your notice arrived late enough to extend the window.
  • After the review board rules, owners can take the dispute to district court or arbitration.
  • Ask the Hunt County tax office or the district for the current rate on your address.

Which exemptions can reduce a Greenville tax bill?

Several, and the Comptroller prints the amounts. The Comptroller prints a mandatory school district homestead exemption and lets any taxing unit add a local one. Older and disabled owners get more, and disabled veterans have a scale of their own.

Texas homestead and disabled veteran exemption amounts printed by the Comptroller
ExemptionAmount as printed
School district residence homestead$140,000
Age 65 or older, or disabled (school districts)Additional $60,000
Disabled veteran, 10 to 29 percent ratingUp to $5,000
Disabled veteran, 30 to 49 percent ratingUp to $7,500
Disabled veteran, 50 to 69 percent ratingUp to $10,000
Disabled veteran, 70 to 100 percent ratingUp to $12,000

Source: Texas Comptroller exemptions and the disabled veteran FAQ.

Hunt CAD publishes a page for people who inherited a home, because heirs missing from the recorded deed must document their interest to qualify. A veteran rated 100 percent can receive a total exemption on a residence homestead.

What permits and local rules apply to a Greenville house?

Greenville's Permits and Inspections Division reviews building permit applications and inspects construction on private property. Permit types include residential construction, pools and accessory buildings, along with electrical, mechanical, plumbing, concrete and energy work, and applications go through the city's online permitting portal.

If a deck, garage or addition went up without a permit, tell the buyer and ask the city how to regularize it. Open permits can surface during title work and slow a closing. Ask the city about short-term rentals and rental registration before you advertise a house for lodging; a clear answer from the planning office beats assuming the city has no rule.

What if someone is living in my vacant Greenville house?

Which side of the state line is the house on?

That question comes first in Texarkana, because the city is two municipalities. A house on the Texas side sits in Bowie County and follows Texas law, while one across State Line Avenue in Arkansas follows Arkansas rules and is recorded in Miller County. This page covers the Texas side.

If yours is a Texas address, a quick sale can take three common forms. Each fits a different situation, and the sections below explain the local pieces that touch all of them.

  • Cash purchase: the buyer pays without a mortgage and can close when your title work is clear.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, with inspections and lender timelines.
  • Sale subject to repairs: the buyer credits you or asks for fixes after an inspection.

How did the Texas half of Texarkana come about?

The Handbook of Texas says the town was established on December 8, 1873, where the Texas and Pacific Railway met the line from Arkansas, and that the Texas railroad laid out its side of the plat from the rail yards to Seventh Street. The Texas city was granted a charter in 1876 and was accorded city status in 1907.

The Handbook describes a town that kept its two halves separate on paper and joined in practice. Each side has its own mayor, council and city officials, while the two share fire service, food and dairy inspection, sewage disposal and some recreation programs. The Federal Building sits across the line and is called the only building of its kind situated in two states.

The same entry names the junction of Interstate 30 and U.S. highways 59, 67, 71 and 82, and ties the local economy to timber, farmland, minerals and railroads. It adds Texarkana College, three major hospitals, the Four States Fair and Rodeo, and Wright Patman Lake. Buyers who work at hospitals or the college, or who commute along I-30, are the natural audience for a Texarkana listing.

How many people does Texarkana, Texas have?

The city's own About Us page, which quotes a 2015 estimate, gives 37,280 people in the Texas city and a metro area spanning all of Bowie County and Miller County, Arkansas. It cites a combined 66,330 for the two cities at the 2010 census and 136,027 for the metropolitan area.

Those figures are older than most sellers would like, so treat them as scale, not as current counts. The takeaway: a Texarkana house competes for buyers across a small two-state metro, where employers on both sides pull workers to either city. Ask a Bowie County title company or the appraisal district for current local counts if you need them for a pricing conversation.

What can a Texarkana listing point to?

Local strengths come from the Handbook of Texas, which calls Texarkana the transportation, commercial and industrial center of the Texas-Arkansas area and a hub reaching into Oklahoma and Louisiana. It names crops such as cotton, corn, rice, soybeans and pecans, and industries from lumber to railroad tank cars and paper products.

  • Education and medicine: Texarkana College, which includes a nursing department, and three major hospitals.
  • Recreation: Wright Patman Lake, Millwood Reservoir across the line, and the annual Four States Fair and Rodeo.

By 1896 the Handbook says the town already had waterworks, an electric light plant, streetcar lines, brick schools and a hotel, which hints at how old some of its neighborhoods may be. If your house is decades old, a buyer will want to see updates to wiring, plumbing and roofing, and records of those updates help.

Bowie CAD's homepage links to a property tax calendar, a truth-in-taxation page on proposed rates, a payment portal and an exemption breakdown. For an exact payoff on your account, use the payment portal or ask the Bowie County tax office.

How do I protest a Bowie CAD appraisal?

The window runs to May 15 or to 30 days after the notice goes out, whichever lands later. Bowie CAD says owners whose market value rose by at least $1,000 receive a notice each spring listing market value, assessed value and taxable value.

  • By mail: P.O. Box 6527, Texarkana, TX 75505.
  • In person: 122A Plaza West in Texarkana or 710 James Bowie Drive in New Boston.
  • Online: through the portal, using the owner ID and PIN printed on the notice.

After filing, you can use an informal meeting with an appraiser, and Bowie CAD says informal meetings begin April 16 with one meeting per property. If you decline the settlement offer, the appraisal review board hears the case. Someone else may represent you if you complete an appointment of agent form.

How do exemptions and caps affect the price a buyer sees?

A homestead exemption lowers taxable value on a main residence, and the state caps homestead appraised value increases at 10 percent a year. Buyers who plan to live in the house will ask what the carrying cost looks like once their own exemption starts.

State rules give school districts a $140,000 homestead exemption, and senior and disabled owners get extra relief plus a school tax ceiling that can follow them to another Texas home. Disabled veterans have their own exemptions, scaled by rating. Apply through Bowie CAD, and ask how to end your own exemption after you sell.

What if I owe back taxes, inherited the house, or face foreclosure?

Unpaid taxes come out of your sale money, and because the lien survives a change of owner, the title company will ask for a payoff. The Comptroller says some collectors allow plans of up to 36 months for homestead owners.

For an inherited house, heirs may go through probate, ask for a muniment of title, or rely on a deed that named a beneficiary and was recorded in the owner's lifetime. For foreclosure, the State Law Library says sales happen on the first Tuesday of a month with 21 days' notice. For squatters, Property Code chapter 24B allows a request to the sheriff or constable, but not against family members or current or former tenants. Talk to a Texas attorney about your case.

Is my Texarkana house governed by Texas or Arkansas law?

By the law of the state where it sits. A Texas-side house is in Bowie County and uses Texas rules. Check your deed and tax bill for the county.

When must I protest my Bowie CAD value?

By May 15, or 30 days after the notice is mailed if that is later. Informal meetings are offered first, then the appraisal review board.

Can I sell a Texarkana house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. The balance, with penalty and interest, comes out of proceeds at closing. Ask the tax office for a payoff good through your closing date.

Do I have to repair a house before a cash sale?

No. Cash buyers commonly take houses as is. A mortgage buyer is likelier to require repairs. Whether you list or sell for cash, gather receipts for any roof, plumbing or electrical work, since both kinds of buyer ask about the age of major systems and a clear paper trail speeds their decision.

Where do I record the deed for a Texas-side sale?

With the Bowie County Clerk, where the land is. Your title company normally handles the filing.

The small-estate route is closed when the estate holds real property other than a homestead.
  • Lender action: a sale notice must precede the first-Tuesday auction by 21 days or more, and a borrower can cure within 20 days of the default letter.

The Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector bills and collects it. Collin Central Appraisal District, in McKinney, sets the value and processes exemptions.

What are the real choices for a Harker Heights owner who wants out quickly?

How did Harker Heights become a city?

The Handbook of Texas Online says the city began in 1957 when two landowners, Pinckney R. Cox and Harley Kern, platted a 400-acre tract along U.S. Highway 190 east of Killeen and sold lots. Buyers wanted water, a system was finished in September 1960, and voters approved incorporation on September 24, 1960, naming the town for Kern.

The city's own history page adds that it started as a general law city and turned into a home rule city in October 1963. In December 1988 it absorbed the 2,200-acre Comanche Hills utility district, taking the townsite from 4,400 acres to 6,600 and adding about 3,500 people. The Handbook calls it a bedroom community without major industry, with schools run by the Killeen Independent School District.

Growth shows up in the Census counts: 26,700 residents in 2010, 33,097 in 2020, and 35,195 for 2025. The city covers 15.61 square miles of land, and it counted roughly 2,120 residents on each of them in 2020. The Handbook also lists four recreation areas, the Killeen Municipal Golf Course and Stillhouse Hollow Lake among the nearby draws, which buyers with families often ask about. Fast growth means most houses are newer subdivision stock, so your buyer will compare yours with others built in the same years.

How does the Bell County appraisal district and tax calendar touch a sale?

State law sets the rhythm. Collectors mail bills near October 1. A balance still open after January 31 turns delinquent, and on February 1 a 6% penalty and 1% interest get tacked on. From there the penalty gains 1% each month and hits 12% on July 1. If the taxing unit hires a collection attorney, a further charge of up to 20% may apply.

What if I inherited the house?

You can still sell it, but the title must show who owns it. Texas lets a will go through probate up to four years after a death, the State Law Library explains. If nobody has to administer the estate, a court order plus the will can be filed as a muniment of title in the clerk's office for the county holding the land.

Some estates use a small estate affidavit. Its checklist: no will, no petition for administration, estate assets worth no more than $75,000 apart from the homestead, every heir on board, and a judge's approval. A third path is the transfer on death deed, which moves a house to named beneficiaries without probate when the owner recorded it before dying.

Heirs preparing to sell should round up the death certificate, any will and the latest tax statement. Ask the Bell County clerk's probate staff which filing fits your family, and expect a buyer's title company to want the recorded paper before it closes.

What should I do about permits and a rental history before I sell?

Ask the city's Planning and Development department about residential permits for any room, deck, carport or garage conversion. Buyers' inspectors and title companies notice unpermitted work, and it can slow the deal or lower the offer.

Did you ever host guests there? Phone the city and find out if a rental registration exists that you should cancel before closing. Tell every buyer about open items. Some cash buyers accept open items as they are, but a buyer with a mortgage may insist on fixing them before funding.

After January 31. The bill goes out around October 1, and a penalty and interest start accruing on February 1. Ask the Bell County tax office for your exact balance and any installment option.

The Bell County clerk. Bell County's clerk. A notary or similar officer has to witness your signature first, and the title company normally takes the signed deed to the clerk after closing.

Usually only with legal authority, for example a court order or an executor's deed. A recorded transfer on death deed or a muniment of title order may do the job too. Ask a Texas attorney or clerk's office staff first.

Water came first. The Handbook of Texas places Del Rio on U.S. Highway 90 near where the Rio Grande meets San Felipe Creek, 154 miles west of San Antonio, with San Felipe Springs supplying millions of gallons that made farming possible in dry country.

Developers formed an irrigation company in 1868 and finished canals in 1871. Locals called the townsite San Felipe del Rio until 1883, when the post office asked for a shorter name. Val Verde County was organized in 1885 with Del Rio as seat, and the town incorporated on November 15, 1911. Population grew from fifty in 1880 to 2,000 by 1890, then to 30,705 in 1990 and 33,867 in 2000.

Early homes clustered near the creek. After the railroad, housing moved north of the rail line, and 1960s retail along Highway 90 pulled growth north again. Amistad Dam and Reservoir, also a 1960s project, drew more housing.

What employers and institutions shape the Del Rio market?

The military, railroad, ranching and border agencies appear throughout the Handbook entry. Laughlin Air Force Base began as a World War II pilot training field, sheep and goat ranchers made Del Rio a hub for wool and mohair, and U.S. Customs, the Border Patrol and the National Park Service have left a mark on the region.

Southwest Texas Junior College and Sul Ross State University have branch campuses, the San Felipe-Del Rio Consolidated Independent School District runs the schools, and a sizable winter Texan group visits each year. The city's own site lists an international airport, an international bridge, a Ports to Plains corridor page, a Main Street program and an economic development corporation among its offerings. Mention those anchors in a listing, and confirm school zoning with the district.

What steps does a Del Rio home project follow with the city?

The Development Services Department reviews plans, issues building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, sign and garage sale permits, inspects work including substandard buildings, and issues certificates of occupancy, per its department page.

Residential submittal steps posted by the City of Del Rio
StepWhat happensWho handles it

The adopted set includes the 2024 International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Plumbing, Fire, Energy Conservation and Fuel and Gas codes, the 2024 Property Maintenance Code and the 2020 National Electrical Code. If an addition or garage conversion went in without a permit, tell the buyer and ask the city what closes the file.

How are Val Verde County property taxes handled in a Del Rio sale?

The Comptroller's calendar shows values fixed on January 1, a lien attaching that day and bills mailed around October 1. A split-payment option allows the first half by November 30 and the second by June 30, though the pay page says most bills are due by January 31.

The city's home page links to its tax department, and the county appraisal district and tax office hold Val Verde County records. If the seller never claimed a homestead exemption, a buyer who closes later in the year may still apply for it. Have the title company show how the year's bill is divided.

What should a Del Rio landlord know before selling a rental?

Texas sets a clear path when a tenant stays. A landlord gives written notice to vacate, normally three days or whatever period the lease sets, then files in justice court. Service is due at least four days before trial, and the hearing falls 10 to 21 days after filing.

An appeal to county court is due within five days of judgment. A writ of possession can issue six days after final judgment, an officer serves it within five days, and 24 hours of notice precede removal, per the State Law Library. Buyers of occupied houses will ask for the lease, deposit records and rent history. Some owners sell with the lease running, and a landlord who plans that route should talk to the tenant about showings early.

What if a Del Rio owner has died or a loan is in default?

Heirs may open probate on a will during the four years after a death, use a muniment of title when no administration is needed, or sign a small estate affidavit if no will exists, the assets total $75,000 or less and every heir agrees. A transfer on death deed signed and filed during the owner's life skips probate.

On a defaulted loan, the lender usually waits until the loan is over 120 days late. You then have 20 days to cure, and a sale notice must be posted three weeks or more ahead of the first-Tuesday auction. Surplus money goes to junior liens, then to the owner. Ask the servicer for an exact payoff first.

Which Del Rio city permits and licenses could come up around a sale?

Besides building permits, Development Services issues garage sale and sign permits, so an estate sale or moving sale may need one. The city home page also lists a business license service, and its business pages include a hotel occupancy tax application and form for lodging operators. If you have rented the house by the night, ask the city whether those pages apply to you before you sell.

For utilities, the city site has utility billing and residential waste collection pages, and recycling and landfill departments. Ask for a final bill and a stop-service date so the buyer starts clean.

The deed itself goes to the Val Verde County Clerk, which records it once it is acknowledged before a notary. Your title company will normally file it and settle the recording charge at closing.

Does Del Rio require a permit for home repairs?

Yes for work covered by adopted codes, such as building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and sign work. Development Services reviews plans, issues permits, inspects and issues the certificate of occupancy.

Who buys houses in Del Rio?

Local employers named in the Handbook of Texas include the military, railroad, ranching, government and border agencies, and winter Texans visit each year. A buyer's financing, an agent's advice or a cash buyer's quote tells you who is active at your price.

Which office files a Del Rio deed?

The Val Verde County Clerk records it after a proper acknowledgment. The title company usually files it and pays the fee from closing funds.

How quickly can a Del Rio eviction finish?

A justice court hearing can come 10 to 21 days after filing, and removal by an officer cannot come until at least six days after judgment. Notice, service and appeal rights add time, so allow several weeks.

Can Del Rio heirs sell without full probate?

Sometimes. Three shortcuts exist: a small estate affidavit, a muniment of title, or a transfer on death deed filed before the owner died. Ask the county clerk and a title company which one a buyer will accept.

Angelina County's seat sits at the crossing of U.S. highways 59 and 69 in the heart of the East Texas Piney Woods. Houses that need work can still find buyers, but they often wait longer on the open market, so list price and condition should be set with that wait in mind.

What shaped Lufkin as a place to own a house?

Lufkin dates to 1882 as a stop on the Houston, East and West Texas Railway, named for a Galveston cotton merchant and city councilman. The Handbook of Texas says the town grew from its rail location and the area's lumber industry, and incorporated on October 15, 1890.

County government moved there too. After a fire destroyed the courthouse at Homer in 1891, Lufkin won a January 2, 1892 election to host it by 1,076 votes to 436. The Handbook divides Lufkin's history into three eras.

Lufkin's three growth eras, per the Handbook of Texas
PeriodDriver

Housing followed those eras. The Handbook says early business centered on Cotton Square behind the depot, where cotton was stored before shipping, so the oldest blocks sit near that rail core while later subdivisions spread outward. An older house may need roofing, wiring or foundation work before a conventional buyer's lender will approve it.

What does Lufkin's economy mean for home buyers?

Lufkin has a diversified base. The Handbook of Texas lists oilfield pumping units, machinery and gears, truck trailers, flooring, foundry products and paper and plywood among its products, and credits Lufkin Industries, founded in 1902, with the city's largest industrial payroll.

It also became a regional trade center in the 1970s, with tourism tied to Sam Rayburn Reservoir, hunting lands and the Ellen Trout Zoo. Between 1965 and 1983 the city added a library, museums, a civic center, a junior college and shopping malls.

For a seller, a mix of industry, services and recreation means buyers arrive from several directions. Households tied to manufacturing and oilfield equipment feel industry cycles, so time a sale to your own needs rather than chasing a peak. The Handbook also records that Lufkin Independent School District saw widespread improvements in that same 1965 to 1983 stretch, and a seller can point buyers to the district's current campuses through the district itself.

Who appraises property in Lufkin, and which taxing units bill it?

The Angelina County Appraisal District values property throughout the county on each January 1 and passes values to the taxing units. Its website lists the City of Lufkin, Angelina County, Angelina College and Lufkin ISD among them, along with Central, Diboll, Hudson, Huntington, Wells and Zavalla school districts and two water districts.

Lumber families drove much of early Lufkin. The Handbook says the Kurth, Henderson and Wiener families formed the Angelina County Lumber Company in 1890, and that Southland Paper Mills and Texas Foundries began as hometown firms in the late 1930s. Many older houses in town date from these industrial decades, and a buyer may ask when major systems were last replaced.

The district maintains ownership records, assigns market value, administers exemptions and special appraisal, and gives information about disputes and appeals. Its community outreach contact is (936) 634-8456, and it asks for at least two weeks' notice for a speaker request.

A Lufkin home usually pays the city, county, college and Lufkin ISD, though a parcel outside city limits will not pay the city. Read the bill to see which units apply.

Which tax dates and exemptions matter in Lufkin?

  • Homestead values rise no more than 10 percent a year after the first exemption year.

From February 1, a late bill picks up a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent monthly interest. If you are selling, have the closing agent divide the year's tax, and request a tax certificate from the Angelina County tax office if a lender or buyer wants one.

What if a Lufkin mortgage payment slips behind?

Move early. Under a Texas deed of trust, the borrower can reinstate within twenty days of a default notice, and the sale notice must arrive three weeks ahead of the auction. The auction is a public sale held monthly, in daytime hours.

Federal rules generally bar a foreclosure start until a home loan is more than 120 days past due. If a sale happens, extra proceeds go to junior lienholders first, then the former owner, and a shortfall suit must be filed within two years.

Selling first lets you pick the buyer, avoid the foreclosure record and keep equity. Ask the servicer for a written payoff.

How do inherited or rented homes in Lufkin get sold?

Title comes first. Probate of a will is open for four years after death. Heirs may rely on a muniment of title, and with no will a small estate affidavit fits assets under a set dollar ceiling, with the homestead left out of the count.

With a renter inside, the landlord usually gives three days' written notice, files in justice court and can seek a writ of possession six days after judgment. Plenty of owners sidestep that sequence by selling while the renter stays. Ask the appraisal district to confirm the owner of record before you sign anything.

Where do Lufkin deeds go?

The Angelina County Clerk records deeds for land in the county, after a notary or similar officer acknowledges the signature. The state clerk manual prices page one at $5.00 and later pages at $4.00, with capped records fees on top. The closing agent usually files and deducts the cost.

Angelina County, where Lufkin is the seat. Its appraisal district values your house and its clerk records your deed.

Yes. A cash buyer accepts the condition, repairs included, and the discount covers the buyer's repair and holding costs. Weigh it against a listing price.

Most unpaid Texas taxes are delinquent on February 1. A six percent penalty and one percent interest apply, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

Is probate required before selling an inherited Lufkin house?

Usually some court or recorded step must show ownership. Routes include probating a will, a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit, or a transfer on death deed that was recorded in the owner's lifetime.

How long does Texas foreclosure take after a default notice?

The borrower has twenty days to cure, and a sale notice comes three weeks before the monthly auction. Selling earlier can protect equity.

Where does Sachse sit, and does the county line change a sale?

Sachse is a suburb about seventeen miles northeast of Dallas, on State Highway 78, and it straddles Dallas County and Collin County. Which side of the county line your lot falls on decides who appraises it and who mails the tax bill.

The state historical association's Handbook of Texas says the settlement was formally established in 1886, when land for a Santa Fe railway right-of-way was donated in exchange for naming the station Sachse. The post office first carried the spelling Saxie and switched to Sachse in 1892. The town became Dallas County's twenty-fifth incorporated place in April 1956 with about 250 residents. By 1914 it had a bank, a Western Union station, three general stores and telephone service. Around 1990 it counted roughly 5,000 residents across both counties, with businesses in publishing and furniture making, and the count reached 9,751 in 2000. Most of that growth came after the 1980s, when Sachse became a residential suburb of Garland, so expect many homes in town to date from that growth period.

What are my choices if I want to sell my Sachse house quickly?

Every route out of a Sachse house swaps something: a retail listing trades time for price, an investor sale trades price for certainty, and a do-it-yourself sale trades money for labor. Listing puts the house in front of the widest crowd, yet the sale hangs on lender timelines and inspection demands. Investor money arrives sooner, and the bid usually lands under what a staged, repaired listing could reach.

A cash buyer makes the most sense when the house is tied up by something outside the market: an inherited home, a tenant, a missed mortgage payment or a move on a tight date. Line up two written bids and read the fine print on closing costs, repair credits and the closing date.

Who sends the tax bill on a Sachse house?

The state itself levies no property tax. Your bill comes from the school district, city, county and similar local bodies, all working from a value the appraisal district fixes each January 1.

A Sachse parcel therefore belongs to either the Dallas Central Appraisal District or the Collin Central Appraisal District. Dallas CAD says it values property for 61 governing bodies and opens its office to the public on weekdays The Collin district publishes its taxing entity information, the exemptions each entity offers and the adopted rates on its own site. Look up your parcel in the correct database first, then read the entity list for your lot.

Statements are mailed in early October; anything unpaid when February arrives counts as delinquent. Because the year's lien attaches on January 1, an unpaid balance rides along with the house.

Schools must deduct $140,000 from a homestead's value, and give seniors and disabled owners another $60,000 deduction. Cities and counties can layer on a percentage exemption of their own. Seniors also get a frozen school tax amount, and veterans with service-connected disability ratings receive graduated or full relief. A separate cap holds yearly appraisal growth on a homestead to 10 percent. File with the appraisal district; Dallas CAD says its homestead filing costs nothing.

Where is a Sachse deed filed?

Record the deed with the clerk of Dallas County or Collin County, whichever holds your parcel.

Texas law accepts a deed for recording only after a notary, another authorized officer or two witnesses has attested the signature. The clerk manual prices the first page at $5.00 and each extra page at $4.00, before the add-on records fees. The title company usually files it after funding. If a sale is part of a probate or a foreclosure workout, tell the closer early so the right documents are in place.

What if a Sachse house is inherited or facing foreclosure?

Both situations come with fixed legal steps, and a buyer will want paper that proves who may sign the deed.

  • Inherited with a will: the will can be probated up to four years after death, and a muniment of title order may let heirs convey without full administration.
  • Inherited without a will: a small estate affidavit covers modest estates, and a court must approve it.
  • Behind on the mortgage: a lender must give a default notice, a 20 day window to catch up, and a sale notice three weeks ahead of an auction held on a first Tuesday.

Selling before the auction date keeps control of the price and any leftover equity. Request a written payoff from the servicer and talk timing through with an attorney or a HUD-approved counselor.

More questions about Sachse, TX

Is Sachse in Dallas County or Collin County?

Both. Sachse spans two counties, so identify the one holding your parcel before asking for tax records.

When are Sachse property taxes due?

Expect the bill in October and pay by January 31. Splitting is allowed, with the halves due November 30 and June 30.

Can I protest my appraisal if I plan to sell?

Yes. The protest goes to the appraisal review board, and the cutoff is printed on your notice of appraised value. A lower value trims the bill that you and the buyer split for the year.

Will a cash sale in Sachse skip the tax bill?

No. Cash buyers settle old taxes at closing just as retail buyers do, because the January 1 lien attaches to the house.

Where do I record the deed for a Sachse house?

File it with the Dallas County or Collin County clerk, depending on the parcel. The deed needs an attested signature and a per-page fee.

Is a quick cash sale realistic in Nacogdoches?

Yes, often within weeks, since nothing waits on a buyer's loan or a listing makeover. The price will sit below a fully renovated listing, so weigh the offer against what repairs, carrying costs and months on the market would cost you.

Nacogdoches is a small East Texas city with a distinct housing market. Per the Census Bureau, only 38.3 percent of homes house their owners, so many houses are rentals, and buyers here include investors as well as families. That helps a seller whose property needs work.

Common reasons owners sell quickly:

  • An inherited house in town that heirs live far from.
  • A rental the owner no longer wants to manage.
  • Age-related repairs on an older home near downtown or the university.
  • A move for work or family.
  • Back taxes or a mortgage that has fallen behind.

What is the Nacogdoches housing market like?

It is a modest-price market tied closely to Stephen F. Austin State University. QuickFacts shows owners' homes at a median $186,000 across 2020 to 2024, rent at $964 and household income at $39,281.

The short commute and the low owner share fit a compact college town. The city has about 27.61 square miles of land, per the same page, so most properties are close to campus, downtown or the major highways.

What shapes the city and its neighborhoods?

Nacogdoches calls itself the oldest town in Texas. The Handbook of Texas places it on State highways 7, 21, 59 and 259 in the central part of the county, and notes hilly terrain with elevations from 150 to 600 feet. Victorian homes line Mound Street, and later subdivisions ring the center of town.

Its history goes back to the Spanish mission of 1716, and Antonio Gil Ibarvo led settlers back in 1779 to lay out the town around El Camino Real and North Street, as the Nacogdoches Central Appraisal District summarizes. Nine flags have flown over the city, and downtown still has red-brick streets and a replica of the Old Stone Fort on the university campus, per SFA's description of the city.

An older house here may carry historic character and a long list of deferred maintenance at the same time. An investor can fold both into the price and spare you the renovation.
