Does Stephen F. Austin State University shape local demand?

Stephen F. Austin State University anchors the local economy and a good share of the rental demand. The Handbook of Texas says the school was established in 1923 as a teachers college and became the community's largest draw for new residents. SFA's own history page calls it the city's most important economic asset and says growth took off in the 1960s as the university expanded.

Other sectors named in the Handbook include agriculture, poultry, manufacturing, trade and tourism. Education and healthcare also show up in the Census data: the clinics and social services sector took in $414.5 million in 2022.

Near campus, ask any buyer whether they plan to rent it, because that affects what they will pay and how much repair they will accept.

Who values and bills a Nacogdoches property?

Nacogdoches Central Appraisal District values property and collects taxes for the county, Nacogdoches ISD, the City of Nacogdoches and other units, according to its website. It offers an online property search, tax payment and protest portal.

The Comptroller's calendar sets the main dates. Values are set on January 1, homestead notices go out around April 1, and most protests are filed by mid-May. Bills arrive around October 1.

  • Taxes unpaid by January 31 become delinquent on February 1.
  • The school district gives a $140,000 homestead exemption, with another $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A tax lien attaches each January 1, so a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid.

Pull your account's exemptions and any unpaid years from the appraisal district first.

What if the house is inherited or in probate?

Inherited houses are common in this market, and the paperwork decides how quickly you can sell. The State Law Library lays out several routes depending on how the owner left the property.

  • Transfer on death deed: record an affidavit of death and the death certificate.
  • Administered estate: the executor or administrator signs the deed.
  • Will with no administration: a court order and the will are recorded as muniment of title.
  • No will and no court case: heirs may use an affidavit of heirship, though buyers and title companies can refuse it.

The library gives four years from death to probate a will. Deeds go on record in the county of the property, so for a Nacogdoches house, call the Nacogdoches County Clerk first, then pick a closing date.

Who tends to buy and live in Nacogdoches homes?

The mix is younger and more mobile than many Texas towns. Census QuickFacts shows 13.0 percent of residents are past 65, 68.2 percent stayed put over the prior year, and the household average is 2.18 people. Median household income is $39,281 and the poverty rate is 31.5 percent, which keeps price points low and makes affordability the main concern for buyers.

The city also promotes its gardens. SFA calls Nacogdoches the Garden Capital of Texas and points to the Ruby M. Mize Azalea Garden, and the Handbook lists nearby Sam Rayburn and Toledo Bend reservoirs. Mature trees and shaded lots can help curb appeal in a showing, though leaf and limb damage after storms is a repair a cash buyer will simply price in.

Because the city covers only about 27.61 square miles of land and holds 1,164 people per square mile, a listing here often competes with several similar houses on nearby streets, so condition and price decide how fast one moves.

Employers named by the Handbook include poultry processors, a fertilizer and feed maker, and a recreational vehicle manufacturer. Jobs in those sectors and at the university keep a steady base of local renters and buyers.

What comes out of the proceeds in Nacogdoches?

Most costs come out of your proceeds at the title company. For a cash buyer, the main items are title and escrow charges, any unpaid taxes, lender payoffs and recording fees.

The County Clerk Manual sets a base recording charge of five dollars for page one, with other clerk fees on top. A notary or other authorized officer must witness the signature before the clerk will record a deed.

Before you agree to anything, ask for the offer price, the closing date and the list of who pays which cost in writing. Set it beside a listing estimate net of commissions and repairs.

More questions about Nacogdoches, TX

What is a typical closing time here?

Usually within a few weeks if title is clean. Inherited or liened properties take longer because the title company has to clear them first. Ask for a target closing date in the written offer.

Must I repair the house first?

No. Cash buyers generally take the property in its current state, and the offer reflects that. You can still compare it with a repaired listing price to see which nets more.

Who bills Nacogdoches property taxes?

Nacogdoches Central Appraisal District values the property and collects taxes for the listed units, including the city, county and Nacogdoches ISD. Use its property search for your account and any balance.

Can a house still titled to a late relative be sold?

Only after the right paperwork is on record. Depending on the situation, that is an executor's deed, a muniment of title order, a recorded transfer on death deed or an affidavit of heirship. A Texas attorney can tell you which fits.

Are Nacogdoches homes mostly rented?

Renters make up a large share. Roughly six in ten homes are rented, per QuickFacts, so investors and landlords are active buyers.

How did Converse turn from farm town to suburb?

The Handbook of Texas says the town was named for a Major Converse, chief engineer of the Southern Pacific Railroad, who bought the townsite tract in 1877. A post office opened in 1878.

The entry describes the community as originally settled by German farmers and says it reportedly had the oldest 4-H Club in Texas by 1990. A singing society, the Salatrillo Liederkranz, was active for many years. By 1946 the population was 175, and by 1965 there were twenty-two businesses and 900 residents.

Growth then arrived quickly. The population was 8,887 in 1990 and 11,508 in 2000, and the Census estimate for 2025 is 32,481. Sellers will find houses of widely different ages here: older homes near the original roads and newer subdivisions built since the 1990s.

When are Bexar County property taxes due for a Converse house?

The Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector says taxes are due in October and must be paid by January 31, with the payment postmarked by that date to be timely. Taxes are delinquent on February 1.

Past-due taxes are surrendered for collection on July 1 and carry an additional 15 or 20 percent collection fee, according to the county page. For business property, jurisdictions may send accounts for collection from April 1.

What payment plans does Bexar County offer Converse owners?

Three plans exist, and your exemptions decide which you can join. A half-payment option splits the base tax between late November and the end of June. A ten-month plan runs October through July for homestead owners holding a disabled, over-65 or disabled veteran exemption, or a qualifying surviving spouse.

The county says its office is the only one in Texas offering the ten-month plan, and it can still be joined in November with 20 percent down. Both groups have options. Owners who are 65 or disabled may file a deferral affidavit with Bexar Appraisal District, and interest accrues at five percent a year. When the owner leaves or stops owning the home, the county says the back taxes and deferred interest fall due on the 181st day.

Service members on active duty outside Texas during a declared war or emergency can defer under Property Tax Code section 31.02(b) by filing form 50-305 with orders. If you hold a deferral, request a payoff figure before listing.

How do I learn what is owed on a Converse house?

Ask for a tax certificate. The county says the fee is $10.00 per certificate, payment is required first, and it shows the status of taxes including penalties and interest if they are delinquent.

Whoever held title on January 1 stays personally liable for that year's tax after a mid-year sale, and the lien stays with the property. For that reason buyers and title companies ask for the certificate before closing, and sellers should pull it early to avoid surprises at the table.

What exemptions help a Converse buyer or seller?

The county lists the general residence homestead, a disabled exemption, a 100 percent disabled veteran exemption and an over-65 exemption. According to the Comptroller, school districts give $140,000 off a homestead, plus $60,000 more at age 65 or for a disability.

For a buyer who closes after January 1, the Comptroller says the exemption can start immediately when the previous owner had none. Applications for the tax year go to the appraisal district, which the county says must be filed before May 1.

The Comptroller cites a Texas Supreme Court opinion on tax sale redemption: homestead owners get two years after the purchaser's deed is filed, and surplus from a tax foreclosure can be claimed by the former owner for two years.

Converse is in northeastern Bexar County, about thirteen miles northeast of downtown San Antonio, on Farm Road 1976 according to the Texas State Historical Association.

Does Bexar County have a ten-month tax payment plan?

Yes. The county says it is the only county in Texas with one, for homesteads with an over-65, disabled or disabled veteran exemption, or a qualifying surviving spouse.

It is a document showing the status of taxes on a property, with penalties and interest if delinquent. The county charges $10.00 per certificate and wants payment first.

Bexar Appraisal District identifies the property, values it and decides exemptions. The tax office bills and collects. Call the appraisal district for exemptions and the tax office for statements.

The Handbook of Texas places the city at State Highway 114 and Farm Road 1709, seventeen miles north of Fort Worth, bordering Grapevine, Keller and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport.

Compare every offer by what reaches you after the loan payoff, taxes and closing costs, since the headline price alone can mislead.

Which counties and appraisal districts cover Southlake?

Southlake straddles two counties, Tarrant and Denton, and the Texas State Historical Association describes it as lying in northern Tarrant and southern Denton counties. The city's tax page links to both the Tarrant County Appraisal District and the Denton County Appraisal District.

Which side of the county line your house sits on decides its appraisal district, tax collector and county clerk. The historical entry counted 6,823 of Southlake's 7,065 residents in Tarrant County and 242 in Denton County in 1990. Check your tax bill or deed for the county name before ordering a payoff or recording a deed.

If your house straddles a boundary or you are unsure, the deed legal description and the tax bill name the county and the taxing units. Share both with the title company at the start of the sale so the right payoff and the right clerk are used.

How did Southlake grow into the city it is today?

Southlake was a scattered rural community that incorporated in the 1960s, with an estimated 1,250 residents in 1966 and 2,031 in 1970. The 1980s brought rapid growth as people left larger cities for a rural setting, lifting the population from 2,808 in 1980 to 7,065 in 1990.

The population tripled by 2000 to reach 21,519, and by 1990 Southlake had become the third largest community in Tarrant County after Fort Worth and Arlington. A large share of today's housing therefore dates from the last four decades, so ask your agent how buyers weigh the age of systems and finishes in your price range.

The entry also lists six manufacturers in 1990 producing engines, concrete products and food packaging, a reminder that the city was not always the residential destination it is now.

Texas now requires each city to post a notice that a parcel's estimated tax appears in the appraisal district's database, and Southlake does that with links to the Tarrant and Denton districts. It also publishes its 2026 tax rate calculation worksheet and offers a form for property tax and budget questions, built to meet a state rule on electronic communication with taxing units. Look up your own parcel in the right district's database rather than relying on a general figure.

Southlake's Building Inspections division reviews plans, issues permits and performs inspections, and it can be reached at (817) 748-8236. Contractors working in the city must register, and general contractors renew each year.

If you finished a basement, built an addition, or replaced a roof or major system, confirm that the work was permitted and passed inspection. A buyer's inspector or lender may ask for proof, and open permits can stall a closing. Southlake's permit system is online, so you can usually look up your address before you list.

Inspection requests submitted by 7:00 a.m. are generally handled the same day, according to the division. The office is at 1400 Main Street, Suite 250.

For sellers this is useful when you need a copy of a permit record, want to confirm a rule before listing, or have a question about a neighbor's project that may affect your sale.

How are the deed and closing records filed for a Southlake sale?

A Southlake deed goes on file with the Tarrant County Clerk or the Denton County Clerk, depending on the parcel's location. The clerk manual from Texas Courts says an acknowledgment by an authorized officer must accompany the signature.

The manual lists a per-page fee plus separate records charges, so the total changes with document length. Your title company can quote it.

With an inherited house, heirs have four years after a death to bring a will to probate. A muniment of title can transfer property under a will where the only debts are liens. The small estate affidavit tops out at $75,000 in assets, not counting the homestead and exempt property.

When a mortgage is in default, the borrower may catch up within 20 days of the default notice. Auctions then follow on a month's first Tuesday after 21 days' notice. Closing a sale before that day protects equity an auction might not.

Look up your parcel in the Tarrant County or Denton County appraisal district database, which the city's tax page links to. Texas law requires that database to show estimated taxes.

Not by law for every sale, but buyers and lenders often ask for it on remodels and additions. Southlake Building Inspections at (817) 748-8236 can tell you whether a permit was closed.

What speeds up a home sale in Alvin?

Selling quickly in Alvin comes down to three things: a clear tax and title picture, honest disclosure of storm and flood history, and a buyer who can close on your timeline. A cash offer is the shortest path when a house needs repairs, has been through water damage, is inherited, or carries a tenant, because the buyer takes the property as it stands.

How does Alvin compare on the Census numbers?

Alvin is a mid-sized, more affordable suburb south of Houston. QuickFacts paints the following picture, with 30,115 residents estimated for 2025, an 11.7% rise over the 2020 base.

Why does Alvin's storm history matter to a seller?

Alvin began as a Santa Fe Railroad flag station in the 1860s near the head of Mustang Slough, on the Galveston-to-Richmond branch. The Texas State Historical Association says Santa Fe hired Alvin Morgan in 1872 to supervise cattle loading at the stock pens, and the settlement took his first name after a postal naming conflict. Alvin was incorporated in 1891 and again in 1893.

Farming and fruit growing carried the early economy, followed by livestock, dairying, rice, oil, natural gas and petrochemicals. The city became an independent school district in 1925 and grew 89 percent between 1960 and 1970, from 5,643 to 10,671 residents. By 2000 it had 21,413.

The same entry notes that each year from July through November Alvin braces for floods, hurricanes and tornadoes. The 1900 Galveston hurricane destroyed or damaged most of the city's businesses and homes, tropical storm Claudette dropped forty-three inches of rain near Alvin in twenty-four hours in 1979, and Alicia battered the area four years later. For a seller, that record is the reason buyers ask about flood history and insurance.

What storm and flood questions will buyers ask in Alvin?

Expect questions about elevation, past water in the house, roof age and wind rating. The City of Alvin's permit page says its adopted codes use a wind load of 140 mph from the code table, and that new construction needs engineer-sealed drawings, a survey and a plot plan.

  • Ask the City of Alvin's engineering and permit staff which flood zone the lot is in, and keep any elevation certificate you have.
  • Keep records of past repairs, including who did the work and whether a permit was pulled.
  • Find out whether the house is covered by flood insurance and what the premium has been.
  • If you rebuilt after storm damage, keep the final inspection record.

Brazoria County also gives owners in a declared disaster area a payment option on their tax bill, described below, which can matter if the house was damaged in a storm that year.

What do Alvin's permit rules mean when I sell?

The City of Alvin requires permits and inspections for new construction, remodeling and repairs. A homeowner who wants to remodel or repair has to show proof of a homestead exemption before buying a permit, so a house that was permitted by a prior owner should have that history on file.

Inspection requests need 24 hours' notice, and permits and inspections go through the city's online MyGov portal. Driveways and driveway culverts need a permit, residential driveways can be 12 to 24 feet wide, and enclosing the front ditch is not allowed. If the property fronts a state highway, TxDOT also has to issue a permit.

If you replaced a driveway, added a room or finished a garage while you owned the house, ask the city's permit office whether the permit was closed. Unclosed permits are one of the common reasons a closing slips.

How do Brazoria County property taxes work for an Alvin seller?

The Brazoria County Tax Assessor-Collector sends tax bills, while the Brazoria Central Appraisal District in Angleton (500 N Chenango Street) values property and processes exemptions. The district keeps weekday hours from eight until four-thirty, and its main line is 979-849-7792.

The county tax office lets owners spread payment in several ways:

  • Half pay: half by November 30, the rest by June 30 of the next year.
  • Age and disability plan: four equal installments, due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31, for qualifying homesteads and unmarried surviving spouses.
  • Disaster plan: the same four installments for owners whose property was damaged in a declared disaster area.
  • Deferral: homeowners 65 or over, or disabled, can postpone payment by signing an affidavit at the appraisal district; 5 percent interest accrues each year.
  • Partial payments: any amount is accepted, and only the unpaid remainder draws penalty and interest.

A deferral comes due once the owner stops owning and living in the home, so a sale triggers it. Tell the title company about any deferral or installment plan early so the payoff figure is right.

A buyer who moves in applies at the appraisal district with a driver's license or state ID showing the property address. A seller with a school tax ceiling can ask the district they are leaving for a certificate to carry the ceiling to a new county.

How does a probate or foreclosure sale work in Alvin?

Filings for an Alvin property go through Brazoria County.

  • Estates: a will should be offered for probate within four years of death. If no administration is needed, heirs can use a muniment of title, filing the court order and will with the county clerk.
  • Mortgage default: on most home loans the lender must wait until the loan is more than 120 days behind, then allow 20 days to cure, then give at least 21 days' notice of the sale.
  • Tax sales: a former owner of a homestead sold at a tax sale has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed to redeem, per a Texas Supreme Court opinion.

Parts of it are, and the city's history includes major storms. The Handbook of Texas says residents face floods, hurricanes and tornadoes from July through November. Ask the City of Alvin which flood zone your lot is in.

Can I pay my Alvin property taxes in installments?

Yes, in some cases. Brazoria County offers a split payment, a four-installment plan for over-65, disabled and disabled veteran homesteads, a four-installment plan for disaster-area owners, deferral for older or disabled owners and partial payments.

Is a permit required for work on my Alvin house?

Yes for new construction, remodeling and repairs, and also for driveways and culverts. Homeowners must show proof of a homestead exemption before buying a permit.

Who sets the value of my Alvin home for tax purposes?

The Brazoria Central Appraisal District. Its office is on N Chenango Street in Angleton, and owners apply there for homestead and age-based exemptions.

With nearly a third of residents under 18, families with children are a large part of the buying pool, so describe nearby schools and parks if you can verify the details. Broadband at 87.4% of households means online listings reach most shoppers.

Who buys in Eagle Pass, and what can they afford?

Mostly local families, so match the price to their budgets. Median household income is $57,207, per capita income is $22,780, and 22.0% of residents live in poverty. Owner costs run $1,570 a month with a mortgage and $499 without, which shows what a typical payment looks like.

The city is young and growing slowly. Its count went from 26,248 in 2010 to 28,130 in 2020, with 12.2% of residents 65 or older and 10.2% under five, so both starter homes and family homes find buyers.

Heritage and language shape marketing. The Census shows 94.2% of residents as Hispanic or Latino, 86.8% of residents aged five and up using another language at home, and 30.2% foreign-born. A bilingual flyer reaches almost the whole market.

Which city permits matter to an Eagle Pass buyer?

The City of Eagle Pass Community Development Department issues them, and its forms page lists many types. Gather the ones that apply to your house before you list.

  • Building permit, commercial or residential, and certificate of occupancy.
  • Electrical, plumbing, mechanical and gas fitting permits.
  • Driveway, right-of-way and tree removal permits.
  • Floodplain development permit and home business permit.
  • Certificate of appropriateness, for property that may fall in a protected area.

The department is at 3295 Bob Rogers Drive, and the permit forms list (830) 773-7781 and planning@eaglepasstx.gov. Call before you drive over to learn how to submit an application. A buyer who plans to run a home business will ask about that permit, and one near the river will ask about the floodplain permit.

How does the Eagle Pass economy touch a house sale?

Retail and services anchor the local economy. Retail sales in 2022 reached about $872 million, or $30,949 per resident, a high figure for a city this size, while health care and social assistance took in near $282 million and food and lodging roughly $123 million.

About 59.4% of residents aged 16 and over work or seek work, and the average commute is 20.1 minutes, shorter than in El Paso or Ennis. That is a fair point to raise with a buyer. Since 92.7% of households have a computer, buyers can browse and sign online, and heirs who live elsewhere can manage a sale by mail and video.

  • Jobs: retail, health care, food service.
  • Commutes: short drives for working families.
  • Remote closing: possible through a title company.

How will Maverick County tax bills affect my Eagle Pass sale?

The appraisal district sets the value, local units set rates, and Maverick County collects. Because the year's lien attaches on January 1, the closing statement divides the bill between you and the buyer.

The Comptroller describes a school exemption for homesteads and extra relief for seniors and disabled owners, plus a limit on yearly value growth for a homestead. If you never applied, ask the appraisal district whether a late filing is possible. Bills arrive in autumn and may be paid in halves, one in late November and one the following June.

  • Ask the county tax office for a balance and a tax certificate.
  • Bring last year's exemption letter to the closing.
  • Dispute a value in the spring, by mid-May.

What if my Eagle Pass mortgage is behind?

You can still sell, and the lender is paid from the proceeds. Texas allows a short window after a default notice to bring the loan current, and the sale notice has to go out weeks before the monthly auction. The State Law Library's foreclosure pages lay out the sequence.

In a city of this size, a buyer who knows the timing can bid fast. Compare any offer with your payoff figure, and get the terms in writing.

What should an Eagle Pass owner collect before taking offers?

A short folder of records speeds a closing in a small city where only a few title offices handle most files.

  • Permits for additions, plus any floodplain or certificate of occupancy paperwork.
  • The latest tax bill and a homestead exemption letter.
  • A lease copy if a tenant lives there, since rent in the city has a median of $880.

Because 60.3% of households own, rentals are common, and some buyers are landlords who want a tenant in place. Say clearly whether you will deliver the house vacant. A vacant house is easier to show but costs utilities and insurance while you wait.

The city forms page also lists a home business permit and a floodplain development permit. If you ran a business from the house or built in a mapped flood area, bring that paperwork, because either fact can come up in a buyer's review.

Keep copies of anything you hand over, and note the date you sent it.

Where is the deed filed, and what if the owner has died?

Deeds for Eagle Pass property go to the Maverick County Clerk after a notary has acknowledged the signature. The clerk's fee schedule changes, so ask for the current one.

For an inherited house, the title company will say which proof of ownership it accepts. The State Law Library describes several court-light routes for smaller estates, and a probate attorney can say which fits your family.

How soon can an Eagle Pass house sale close?

The date comes from the buyer and the title company, so get one in writing. Clear title and a ready payoff letter help.

Does the City of Eagle Pass publish permit forms?

Yes. Its forms page lists building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, driveway, floodplain and certificate of occupancy applications.

Who collects property tax on an Eagle Pass home?

Maverick County collects it, and the appraisal district sets the values. Ask the county tax office for your balance.

Can I sell an Eagle Pass house with a lien?

Yes, if the lien is paid at closing. Ask the lienholder for a payoff letter before you accept an offer.

Where is Katy, and which county handles my house?

Katy sits west of Houston and its city limits reach into Fort Bend, Harris and Waller counties, so the county that appraises and taxes your house turns on where the parcel sits. Look at your tax statement to see which county it names.

The city's demographics page gives its land area as 15.35 square miles. Fort Bend Central Appraisal District runs a parcel search and an online map where you can confirm a property, and its tax assessor-collector sends the bills for that county. For a Harris or Waller parcel, use that county's own appraisal district and tax office instead.

How fast has Katy grown, and how does that touch a seller?

Katy has grown from about 8,000 residents in 1990 to a city estimate of 28,121 for 2025. More buyers moving in has meant steady demand for houses, but also a lot of newer competing listings nearby.

The same page lists 7,490 households in a 2023 estimate, up from 4,336 in 2010. The city's own description of itself pairs old town heritage with new families and businesses, and that mix shows up in the housing stock: older homes near downtown and much newer subdivisions around them.

Where did Katy's older neighborhoods come from?

The first settlement, called Cane Island after the creek, dates to 1872, and the town site was platted in 1895 along the railroad. The first post office came in 1896, and the town rebuilt after the 1900 hurricane flattened most of its buildings.

Rice was the main crop for years, with peanuts and cotton alongside it. Katy Independent School District formed in 1918, a gas field was found in 1934, and Katy became a city in 1945. In 1986 a local committee placed historical markers on more than a dozen older homes and buildings downtown. If your house is one of those older downtown properties, ask the city planning staff what rules apply before you order exterior work.

Which schools serve Katy houses?

Katy ISD serves the city, and the district campuses inside city limits are the ones buyers will ask about first.

  • Katy Elementary, Hutsell Elementary and WoodCreek Elementary
  • Katy Junior High and WoodCreek Junior High
  • Katy High School
  • Miller Career and Technology Center and the Opportunity Awareness Center

Aristoi Classical Academy, a free public charter school for kindergarten through 12th grade, also operates here. Attendance zones shift, so buyers should ask the district for the campus assigned to your address.

Which repairs on a Katy house call for a city permit?

Yes for most structural, mechanical and outdoor work. The city's Permit and Building Services division requires a permit for new construction, remodeling, roofing, heating and cooling systems, electrical and plumbing, and any job that adds or removes walls.

Pools, hot tubs, storage buildings, carports, garages, driveways, sidewalks, patios, irrigation, water heaters, demolition and house moving are on the permit list too. The city says it has adopted the 2021 International Building Codes and the 2026 National Electrical Code. Applications, plan uploads, fee payments and inspection scheduling run through an online portal, and a card payment carries a convenience fee of 3.95 percent or $3.00, whichever is greater.

Unpermitted work is a common snag at inspection. If a prior owner finished a garage or added a patio without a permit, a buyer using a loan may balk, while an investor paying cash will usually just price the risk in.

How do Texas property taxes affect a sale in Katy?

The lien dates from the first of January and the bill follows around the first of October, so the day you close decides who carries which part of the year's bill.

  • Appraisals reflect value and ownership as of January 1 (Texas Comptroller).
  • Bills are mailed about October 1, and most unpaid balances turn delinquent on February 1.
  • Protest cutoffs fall on May 15 in most years, with a 30-day alternative for late notices.
  • Homestead appraisals are capped at a ten percent yearly rise.

Fort Bend CAD offers online homestead filing and appeals by mail, office visit or online.

What are my choices if I need to sell fast in Katy?

Three routes are open to a Katy seller, and the calendar and repair budget usually pick one.

  • A listed house is seen by the most buyers, though it means open houses, a repair list and weeks of waiting.
  • Doing it yourself keeps the commission but hands you the contract work and the marketing.
  • Buyers paying cash skip the lender appraisal, so they can accept the property unrepaired and close when you say.

For a Katy house with deferred maintenance, renters still living there or an estate not yet settled, the cash route removes the repair list. Weigh every offer against what a listing would really net once commission and repairs come out.

How does the deed get recorded after a Katy sale?

Deeds go to the clerk in Fort Bend, Harris or Waller County, whichever one holds the parcel. The state clerk manual wants the signature witnessed by a notary first, and it prices filing by the page with extra records charges. Title companies normally record for you, so ask for the final amount on your settlement statement.

What if my Katy house is headed for a tax auction?

When taxes go unpaid long enough, the taxing unit can sue and the property can be sold at a tax foreclosure auction, usually run by the constable or an agent hired by the unit. Texas has no single statewide list of these auctions, so watch the county clerk and county tax office sites for Fort Bend, Harris or Waller.

An owner can still buy the property back in some cases. For a homestead, farm or mineral interest, the Texas Supreme Court has described a two-year window from the date the buyer's deed is filed, with a 25 percent premium in the first year and 50 percent in the second, plus the bid, recording fee, taxes, penalties and costs. Other property gets 180 days at a premium of up to 25 percent. Any money left over after the sale belongs to the former owner, who has two years from the sale to claim it.

Should you owe back taxes here, a sale before any suit usually costs far less than letting it reach auction, because court costs and attorney fees are added to the bill along the way.

What should I tell a buyer about Katy's older downtown?

Downtown Katy still has houses from the town's early decades, and the 1986 markers on a dozen or more historic homes and buildings make a good walking tour for out-of-town buyers. Mention the history in your pitch if the house has period details, and ask city staff whether any local review applies before changing a front elevation.

The city also publishes a water conservation stage notice on its home page, and a stage 1 mild notice was posted there in August 2026. Buyers from outside the area appreciate hearing how watering is handled before they close on a lawn-heavy lot.

What if I owe on the mortgage or just inherited this Katy house?

A missed-payment spiral in Katy follows the Texas non-court route: a default letter, a short window to bring the loan current, then a posted and recorded sale notice and a first-Tuesday auction. The State Law Library walks through each stage, and a housing counselor can tell you where your loan stands.

If a relative left you the house, check whether a will exists and whether anyone opened probate. Heirs who want the homestead tax break must show the appraisal district proof of kinship and the death certificate. A lawyer in Harris, Fort Bend or Waller County can tell you which deed route fits.

More questions about Katy, TX

Is Katy in Harris County or Fort Bend County?

Both, and Waller County as well. The city limits extend across three counties, so the county on your tax statement tells you which appraisal district and tax office apply to your house.

Is a roofing permit needed in Katy?

Yes. The city's Permit and Building Services division lists roofing among the work that needs a permit, along with remodeling and heating and cooling replacement. Apply through the city's online portal.

What is Katy's current population?

The city's demographics page shows a 2025 estimate of 28,121, up from 21,894 counted in 2020. The same page lists 7,490 households as a 2023 estimate.

By what date must a Katy owner protest the appraisal?

The usual cutoff is May 15 unless the notice arrived late, in which case you get 30 days from delivery. File with the appraisal district for the county where your parcel lies, such as Fort Bend CAD, which accepts filings online.

Will anyone buy a Katy house with unfinished repairs?

Yes, with a buyer who takes it as-is; a loan buyer will likely ask for repairs after the inspection. Unpermitted work is worth disclosing and sorting out early, since it can slow a loan-backed sale.

Where is Royse City and how did the town start?

Royse City is on State Highway 66 about five miles northeast of Rockwall, in the northeastern corner of Rockwall County, and parts of it lie in Collin and Hunt Counties as well. That three-county layout is the first thing to understand before you sell.

According to the Texas State Historical Association, the town was named for G. B. Royse, who platted the townsite in 1886, and settlement began in 1885 when the Missouri, Kansas and Texas Railroad was planned through the area. Early residents and businesses moved over from nearby Fate, which the railroad bypassed. By 1890 the community had about 1,000 people, two cotton gins and a gristmill. It was first incorporated in 1891, voted out in 1902 and reinstated in 1906.

The population stayed near 1,000 to 2,000 for most of the twentieth century and reached 2,957 in 2000. The city's recent budgets show much faster growth in taxable value, which is why houses here now trade in a market shaped by newer subdivisions around older downtown blocks.

Its railroad origin explains why the older core sits where it does. The Texas State Historical Association notes that the community counted forty businesses by 1896 and that local schools had four teachers and 204 students by 1898, and that trade in cotton, cottonseed oil and ginning drove the early twentieth century economy.

Why does it matter that Royse City sits in three counties?

It determines which appraisal district values your house and which county clerk records your deed. The city's budget says the Rockwall, Collin and Hunt County appraisal districts each certify values for property inside the city, and Rockwall CAD compiles the three rolls.

These figures describe taxable value for a past fiscal year, not what a house sells for, so use them as context only. For a current tax rate, ask the tax office of the county your house is in, because that office bills the combined rate.

Which Royse City permit rules should you check before listing?

No permit is needed to sell, but the city says building permits must be obtained before any improvement or alteration to a property. If you have finished a project, such as a pergola, flatwork or electrical change, confirm it was permitted.

The Building Inspection department can be reached at 972-524-4710 or permits@roysecity.com.

How does the MyGov permit system affect a Royse City house?

The city says you can apply for permits, register contractors, pay fees and follow project status through MyGov. If a previous owner or a contractor did work, you can ask building inspections whether the permit was closed.

The department handles building, zoning and property maintenance ordinances, including fencing, yards and open space. Plan review can take up to 10 business days, and approval goes to the project contact by MyGov or email. Payment can be made through MyGov, by mail or at City Hall. Royse City also publishes permit guides for flatwork, arbors, pergolas and gazebos, and new single-family dwellings, and these state that no work may begin until the permit is issued and approved plans must be on site for inspection. If you are selling a house with a recent addition, a closed permit is a useful document for a buyer's lender or inspector.

A short checklist before you list: gather permit numbers for any addition, fence, flatwork or electrical change, confirm each was inspected, and keep the approval email or MyGov record. How do property taxes and exemptions work when you sell in Royse City?

Texas sets one tax calendar for every city, and one statewide homestead rule limits yearly increases in appraised value. The Comptroller prints school district homestead exemptions and the age and disability add-ons, and your appraisal district can show which exemptions are on your house.

A buyer who moves in after January 1 can get the exemption for the rest of that year if the prior owner had none. If a closing falls between the November 30 and June 30 halves of a split payment, the title company confirms what is paid.

What if the house has a lien, a tenant or an estate?

A lien, a tenant or an estate each has its own filing route.

  • Tax lien: unpaid tax follows the property and has to be paid before closing.
  • Tenant: a written notice to vacate comes first, then a justice court suit.
  • Estate: the route may be a beneficiary deed, a court-approved muniment, an affidavit of heirship or an administrator's deed.

The deed is recorded with the clerk of the county where the parcel sits, which here could be Rockwall, Collin or Hunt.

The city has guides for flatwork and for arbors, pergolas and gazebos, so call 972-524-4710 before assuming no permit applies.

Up to 10 business days, according to the city. Feedback goes through MyGov or by email to the contact on the application, and payment can be made online, by mail or at City Hall.

Sometimes. Whether a beneficiary deed, muniment of title or affidavit of heirship applies depends on the paperwork, and a title company can say which one a buyer's lender will accept.

After January 31, according to the Texas Comptroller, with penalty and interest starting February 1.

What makes selling a house in Lake Jackson, TX different?

Lake Jackson is a planned city, so many houses sit on curved streets under mature oaks, and buyers often care about lot, trees and drainage as much as the floor plan. A seller who explains the neighborhood and the Brazoria County tax picture sells with fewer surprises.

The city's own history says Lake Jackson began in 1941 when Dow's Texas Division planned a complete new town on the old Lake Jackson Plantation site for its plant workers. Construction started December 8, 1941, and the city incorporated on March 14, 1944.

How was Lake Jackson laid out?

An architect planned the roughly 1,300-acre town on paper before clearing began, and the city says he asked that as many trees as possible be spared. Streets are called drives, ways and streets: drives circle the outskirts as through routes, streets end at drives or ways, and ways lead downtown.

Streets are named for flowers, fruits, shrubs and trees, and the city lists quirks like This Way and That Way. The Handbook of Texas adds that the town includes Jackson Lake, Flagg Lake and two other lakes, and that its first school opened in 1943 before the Brazosport Independent School District formed in 1944.

  • Curved streets give each lot its own shape, so check survey lines before listing.
  • Tree roots are a common concern on oak-lined lots, so ask an inspector to check foundation and sewer lines.
  • Older homes near downtown pre-date later codes, so gather any permit records.

What do buyers ask about the Brazosport area?

They ask about jobs, schools and storms. The Handbook of Texas says the town became part of the Brazosport industrial area, with a regional mall opening in 1976 and the South Freeway speeding growth. The city adopted a home-rule charter in 1954, and the 2000 Census population was 26,386 as the city's history reports.

The Handbook also lists the Brazosport Center for the Arts and Sciences and Wilderness Park, which extends to the Brazos River bank. The Brazosport Independent School District serves the community, so confirm zoning for your address.

How did Lake Jackson grow after Dow built it?

The city says its first residents moved into the 200-unit Oak Wood Project in January 1943, bought groceries from Clute and Freeport, and picked up mail at a trailer branch near a plant. The population went from zero at the start of 1943 to about 1,800 by April 1944, and later reached 2,897 in 1950 and 11,090 in 1958, according to the Handbook of Texas.

The Handbook lists 19,102 residents in 1980, 22,776 in 1990 and 26,386 in 2000. Growth followed the opening of a regional mall in 1976 and the completion of the South Freeway.

For a seller, that history means a Lake Jackson house may date from the postwar boom or from later decades, so check the build year on your appraisal record. Older houses can carry foundation, plumbing and wiring questions. A pre-listing inspection costs less than a failed contract, and the report gives buyers a baseline.

If your house sits near one of the town's lakes, ask the city and county about drainage records and any flood zone designation, since buyers and lenders will ask.

How do Brazoria County tax payment options affect a Lake Jackson sale?

Source: Brazoria County Tax Office.

What happens to deferred or unpaid taxes when I sell?

Deferred taxes and interest come due when the owner no longer owns and lives in the home, so a sale triggers payment. The county says unpaid deferred debt can bring penalties and legal action by taxing units.

A tax lien attaches to Texas property on January 1 for that year's taxes. Ask the Brazoria County Tax Office for a certificate listing every account on your parcel, then give it to the title company early.

State law sets the calendar, and Brazoria County collects. Penalty and interest begin on February 1 on bills unpaid by January 31, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

  • Homestead applications are due by April 30, and school districts give $140,000 off value for a homestead.
  • Protests go to the appraisal review board by May 15, unless the notice arrived late.
  • Tax bills go out in October and are due when received.
  • Elderly or disabled owners can also ask for a school tax ceiling.

The state details are on the Comptroller deadlines page and the exemptions page.

Which repairs matter before listing in Lake Jackson?

Buyers in a coastal county tend to look at roofs, drainage, windows and foundation first. Check with the city's permit office before major work, and keep invoices.

If repairs are too costly or the timeline is short, a cash buyer will purchase as-is and handle the work after closing. Compare that against what you would net after repairs, commissions and carrying costs.

What does Lake Jackson deed recording cost?

Brazoria County's clerk records deeds for Lake Jackson land. The county clerk manual lists a records management fee of up to $10, a records archive fee of up to $10 and a technology fee of $2.00, added to the per-page charge.

A signature must be acknowledged by a notary or similar officer first. Your title company handles filing.

Who should I ask about my Brazoria County account?

Start with the Brazoria County Tax Office, which collects the bill, and the Brazoria County Appraisal District, which handles exemptions. Ask each for a written account summary that shows the exemption status, any installment plan or deferral on file, and any back taxes.

Hand those papers to the title company as soon as you have a contract. If an installment plan is open, find out whether the buyer must pay off the plan balance or the title company will settle it from your proceeds. Payoff figures change with the closing date, so request an updated figure for the closing day.

More questions about Lake Jackson, TX

Who bills the tax on a Lake Jackson house?

The Brazoria County Tax Office collects it after the Brazoria County Appraisal District sends the certified roll. Bills go out in October.

When are Lake Jackson taxes delinquent?

Taxes unpaid after January 31 are delinquent, with penalty and interest starting February 1. Texas law raises the penalty to 12 percent on July 1.

Can I pay Brazoria County taxes in installments?

Yes, in several cases. Half can be paid by November 30 and half by June 30, and owners 65 or older, disabled or disabled veterans can pay in four installments.

Does selling end a Brazoria County tax deferral?

Yes. Deferred taxes and interest come due when the owner no longer owns and lives in the home.

When was Lake Jackson incorporated?

The city incorporated on March 14, 1944, after Dow planned the town in 1941 for plant workers. It adopted a home-rule charter in 1954. The city's founding plan set aside about 1,300 acres, and the layout of drives, ways and streets still guides how people find their way around.

What are the quickest ways for a Balch Springs owner to sell?

An owner here can put the house on the market, find a buyer without an agent, or accept a cash bid from someone who will take it in its present shape and close when you say. The best fit hangs on the house's condition, any liens or city notices attached to it, and how soon you need the funds.

This is a city of owners. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates show 64.7 percent of homes occupied by the people who own them, with 3.29 people in the average household. Many sales here involve family homes held for decades, houses that came through an estate, or rentals that a landlord is tired of managing.

  • Market listing: works if the house shows well and a lender signs off on the buyer.
  • Investor purchase: skips showings and loan approval, and usually the repair list too.
  • Payoffs first: a mortgage, tax balance or code fine is paid from the proceeds, so get each figure in writing before you accept anything.

Where did Balch Springs come from, and why are its houses mostly postwar?

Balch Springs began as a cluster of farms around a spring and became a commuter suburb of Dallas, which is why most of its houses date from the postwar decades. The Texas State Historical Association says the community was founded around 1870 when the family of John Balch settled by three springs, one of which never ran dry.

Residents incorporated the town on June 13, 1953, with a mayor-council government, in order to avoid annexation by Dallas. The population was about 3,500 in 1956, 13,050 by 1976, 17,406 in 1990 and 19,375 in 2000. Interstate 635 made the drive to Dallas faster in the 1970s, and by the late 1970s about 95 percent of working residents commuted to Dallas or Garland.

The town sits on Interstates 635 and 20 and U.S. Highway 175, ten miles southeast of Dallas in Dallas County. Hickory Creek rises here. By 1991 the town had seventeen manufacturers, including makers of shipping pallets and machine parts. In 1988 residents voted to combine with Mesquite, but the vote was ruled invalid and Balch Springs remained independent. In earlier decades children attended school in either the Dallas or Mesquite districts, so ask the county appraisal district which school district taxes your parcel.

How do Balch Springs household and housing figures compare with other places?

A typical owned home in Balch Springs was valued at $224,400 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and a typical renter paid $1,378 a month. The city's population estimate for mid-2025 is 27,258, which is 1.6 percent under the 27,705 baseline for April 2020 but well above the 23,728 counted in 2010.

Does Balch Springs require rental registration or a certificate of occupancy?

  • Rental registration: the applicant needs a driver's license and proof of ownership, such as closing paperwork or a deed in the applicant's name. The registration must be renewed every two years.
  • Inspection timing: the city says rental inspections must be done before a tenant moves in, or the owner incurs a violation fee.
  • Certificate of occupancy: the applicant provides a driver's license, a lease or proof of ownership, a site map and a floor plan.

Because registration is tied to the owner's name and deed, an investor who keeps the tenant files a new registration once the deed is recorded. Contact the Permits and Inspections Division at 972-286-4477 to ask what is on file for your address. Inspection requests are sent by email to inspections@balchspringstx.gov, per the city's permits page.

What city permits and sign-offs come up when a Balch Springs house changes hands?

The city's permit sheet shows what a seller or investor buyer may need: a certificate of occupancy takes a lease or proof of ownership, a site map and a floor plan, while electrical, plumbing and air conditioning work each need their own permit pulled by a registered master contractor. Roof work can be a same-day permit when no structural work is involved, and the sheet lists the current codes as the 2021 IRC and IBC and the 2020 NEC.

For an estate or moving sale, note the garage sale rules on the same sheet: three sales a calendar year, with 90 days between them. Contractors working on the house must be registered with the city, so check that anyone you hire for pre-sale repairs is on the list. Reach Permits and Inspections at 972-286-4477, and send inspection requests to the email address on the city's permits page.

Can an open city notice get in the way of selling in Balch Springs?

An open notice is not a bar to selling, but it stays with the property and ought to be cleared or discussed before closing. Officers walk the neighborhoods every day and also act on complaints.

The first letter allows 10 days to fix the problem, shortened to 7 days for tall grass and solid waste, and it remains active for 12 months. If a return visit finds no change, the officer writes a Notice to Appear that lists the ordinance, the fine and how to reach the court. Owners can ask the department for more time to complete a repair.

Before you list, walk the lot with the city's Top 10 violations list, which the Code Enforcement page offers in English and Spanish. Disclose any citation or court date to a buyer, so the closing is not held up.

How much time do I have to sell before a foreclosure auction?

Most Texas home loans can be foreclosed without a lawsuit, and the calendar is strict enough that a sale before the auction is often workable. Federal servicing rules generally hold off a first filing until the loan is over 120 days delinquent.

  • A borrower can reinstate by paying what is past due within 20 days after the default notice arrives.
  • The servicer then sends a sale notice at least 21 days ahead, posts it at the courthouse and files it with the county clerk.
  • Auctions run on a month's first Tuesday, with a window from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m.
  • A lender can sue for a shortfall within two years, and the borrower can ask for a credit for the home's fair market value.

The Dallas County commissioners court sets where auctions are held, so ask the county clerk for the spot. A sale that closes before the first Tuesday can pay off the loan from the proceeds. The State Law Library's foreclosure guide walks through each stage.

How does a tenant change the sale of a Balch Springs house?

Give each buyer a copy of the lease, since its terms govern what a new owner can do about the occupant. If you need the tenant gone before closing, a written notice to vacate normally allows at least three days unless the lease sets another period.

An eviction suit goes to justice court. The tenant must be served four days or more before trial, and a hearing is set 10 to 21 days after filing. A losing party can appeal to county court within five days, and a writ of possession waits at least six days after final judgment. Many owners with tenants simply pick a buyer who will keep the tenant, which skips that timeline.

More questions about Balch Springs, TX

Must I keep my rental registered until the Balch Springs sale closes?

Yes, while the house is rented. The registration lasts two years and requires an inspection before a tenant moves in. A buyer who keeps renting registers in their own name with proof of ownership.

How soon must a Balch Springs code notice be fixed?

Ten days for most notices and seven days for tall grass or solid waste. If a return inspection still finds the problem, a citation with a fine and court date follows. A written extension request is allowed.

Where is the deed filed for a Balch Springs sale?

With the Dallas County clerk, since the city lies in Dallas County. The deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer.

Is it too late to sell once the lender posts a foreclosure notice?

Not if the sale closes first. The borrower has 20 days from the default notice to reinstate, and the lender owes at least 21 days' notice of sale. Count back from the first Tuesday of the month.

How many people call Balch Springs home?

An estimated 27,258 people as of July 2025, in 8,247 households counted in 2020-2024. That is 1.6 percent below the April 2020 baseline, across 9.02 square miles.

A Denison seller has three paths: hire an agent to list, find a buyer alone, or go to a buyer who pays cash. Speed, repair cost and final price pull against each other, so rank them before you take any call.

Denison is a railroad town. The city's FAQ says it was established on September 23, 1872 and incorporated on March 7, 1873, and that it was named for a Katy Railroad vice president who never came to Texas. It sits in Grayson County and the city puts its population at roughly 28,000. A smaller city means a smaller pool of listing buyers, and houses with deferred maintenance can sit longer than they would in a big metro.

The Grayson County Tax Assessor-Collector bills and collects it, and the Grayson County Appraisal District sets the value. The city's tax rates page lists the main office at 100 W Houston in Sherman and a Denison office at the County Sub-Courthouse at 101 W Woodard, and puts the appraisal district at 205 N Travis Street in Sherman.

The same page lists these rates per hundred dollars of value, under a 2025 tax year heading. Read the table as the city prints it, and ask the county tax office for the rates that apply to your own bill, since they can differ by property.

What does Denison require before I renovate or hand over a house?

Denison's building department issues permits for most structural work, and the city's FAQ lists several that sellers often overlook. A permit is needed for any new fence, a replacement fence, or a repair involving 20 feet or more of fence, and for every detached storage building or shed regardless of size.

A building permit stays valid while work continues, and expires if work is suspended or abandoned for 180 days after it was issued or after the last approved inspection. The FAQ also says a homeowner can pull a homeowner permit for an owner-occupied single-family home only if the property is homestead-exempt as verified through the appraisal district. If it is a rental or not homestead-exempt, the applicant must register as a general contractor and cannot do electrical, plumbing or mechanical work that needs a state license.

For work that needs a permit, the FAQ says the application usually asks for a scope of work with materials, owner and contractor contact details, a site plan or drawing, and a registered contractor. Texas law sets fixed steps for both situations, and a quick sale is possible in either one if the paperwork is ready. For an inherited house, a will has a four-year probate window. For a mortgage in default, the lender sends a notice of default and you may reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days. The auction notice follows, with the public sale held in a morning-to-afternoon window on a first Tuesday. Ask the Grayson County clerk where foreclosure notices are posted.

Closing before the sale date stops the foreclosure on that loan. Ask your servicer for a payoff statement in writing.

Where does a Denison deed get filed?

A notary witnesses the signature, and the Grayson County clerk, who keeps the land records, files the deed. Under the Texas Courts clerk manual, a conveyance without a proper acknowledgment is not eligible for recording.

The title company will quote the clerk's recording charges for your deed. Your title company will quote the final total. A Denison house is filed in Grayson County, the county of the land, even though a branch tax office sits in town.

Before you list, gather the last deed, your tax receipts and any lien releases. A missing document can hold up a closing, and the closing agent will want to see each one.

The department's FAQ also describes certificates of occupancy for new buildings and tenant spaces. That rule mainly reaches commercial property, so the owner of a mixed-use building downtown should ask the department which applies. Permit payments in person are taken by cash or check at the Building Inspections office, with cards accepted through the online portal.

Yes. The city's page lists a combined rate of 2.318114 for the tax year it labels 2025, built from the city, school district, county and college rates. Ask the county tax office for the figure on your own bill.

Is a permit needed for a shed or fence in Denison?

Yes for a shed of any size, and for a new fence or a repair covering 20 feet or more. The city asks for a site plan with dimensions from the property lines.

February 1, for taxes not paid by January 31. Penalty and interest begin to accrue at that point.

How would you describe Saginaw to a buyer?

Saginaw is a residential and commercial city on State Highway 496, about ten miles northwest of Fort Worth in Tarrant County, so a house here is priced and marketed as part of the Fort Worth suburban ring.

The Handbook of Texas traces the area to a farm settlement once called Dido. Three railroads crossed it in the 1880s, and in 1882 the community took the name Saginaw from the Michigan hometown of a local landowner. A mill and elevator company and an aircraft maker arrived around 1936, the city incorporated in 1949, and the population climbed from 561 in the late 1950s to 8,551 in 1990, 12,374 in 2000 and 23,890 in 2020. By 2023 the state record counts 556 businesses in the city.

  • Investor bids suit houses needing work.
  • A polished house can do better on the open market.
  • All of Saginaw sits in one county, which keeps tax paperwork simple.

Which sale route fits a Saginaw owner?

Saginaw owners generally pick among a brokered listing, a no-agent sale and an as-is investor purchase, and the choice follows your calendar and your repair budget.

Brokered sales draw the biggest pool of bidders and tend to net the most for a house in good order, with weeks of showings and loan approvals as the cost. Going without a broker keeps the commission in your pocket and hands you the photos, contract and negotiation. An investor can fund on a date of your choosing without a lender appraisal, and the bid is shaded for repair and resale costs. Ask every buyer to put the price, closing costs and closing date in writing.

  • Listing fits a tidy house and a loose schedule.
  • An investor sale fits a house weighed down by repairs, occupants, an estate or a tax debt.
  • Collect more than one bid and compare what lands in your account.

Who taxes and appraises a Saginaw home?

Tarrant Appraisal District sets your home's value; the rates come separately from each taxing unit, so the bill adds up several levies instead of one city figure.

TAD states that it serves seventy-three taxing units countywide, including the county, cities and school districts, which pay for police, fire, schools, streets and water systems from the revenue. It also states that filing an exemption costs nothing. Its site notes that 2026 notices of appraised value have already gone out in a new layout. Valuation is pegged to January 1, and an owner who disagrees files a protest by the deadline shown on that notice.

What property tax dates affect a Saginaw seller?

Four dates carry the most weight: January 1 for the lien, May 15 for protests, October 1 for bills and January 31 for payment.

The Comptroller calendar lists the rest.

How much extra do late taxes cost on a Saginaw house?

Late tax compounds fast, starting at a 6 percent penalty with 1 percent interest in February and ending at a 12 percent penalty by July.

The interest rate runs without a ceiling, and a unit's collection lawyer may add a fee of up to a fifth of the tax. If you sell with tax still owing, the closer settles it out of your check. Homestead owners can request a payment plan, which some offices extend to three years, and senior or disabled owners may spread the current bill over four installments.

Which exemptions apply to a Saginaw homestead?

The base homestead exemption applies to the home you live in, and added relief exists for age, disability and veteran status.

Schools deduct $140,000 from a homestead, plus another $60,000 for seniors and the disabled, and a state cap stops the appraised value of a homestead from jumping more than 10 percent in a year. Veterans see deductions that scale with their rating, between $5,000 and $12,000, and a full 100 percent rating carries a total exemption on the homestead. Heirs without a recorded deed in their name must bring an ownership affidavit, the death certificate and a current utility bill.

What do I need to transfer and record a deed in Saginaw?

Real property records for Saginaw are kept by the Tarrant County clerk, and that office takes the deed.

A notary or another officer with acknowledgment powers must witness the signature before the clerk will accept it. The clerk manual sets a five dollar charge for the opening page and four dollars per page after it, plus smaller add-ons. The title company ordinarily handles the filing, and a lender's lien release goes through the same office.

What if I am behind on my Saginaw mortgage?

Most Texas home loans carry a power of sale, so the lender can auction a house without a lawsuit, on a first Tuesday.

The first paper is a default notice that gives twenty days to catch up. A sale notice follows no later than three weeks before the auction and goes on the courthouse door and into the clerk's records. Federal rules hold off a start until a home loan is past 120 days late. A sale on your own terms can save equity, so call the servicer and a counselor early. If an auction falls short of the debt, the lender has two years to sue for the gap.

How does an inherited Saginaw house get sold?

The path turns on whether the owner left a will, since a buyer needs a deed or court order showing exactly who can sign.

  • Will: offer it for probate within four years of the death.
  • Will with no debts to administer: a muniment of title order, recorded with the clerk where the house stands.
  • No will and a small estate: an affidavit, available when assets other than the homestead come to $75,000 or less and a judge approves.

How did Belton start out, and why does the creek matter to older lots?

A history the city publishes, written by a former librarian, says surveyors laid the town out in August 1850 as county seat of the newly organized Bell County. The first name was Nolandville; by 1851 it was Belton, and the town incorporated in 1852.

Nolan Creek ran near the courthouse square, and the first courthouse stood on blocks to ride out floods. A flood in 1913 is why one city park bears a family name. The 2020-2024 midpoint for an owner-occupied Belton home is $258,700, and 56.0% of units are lived in by owners. Tenants pay a midpoint of $1,252 monthly, so rentals are a real part of the supply.

Apply from January 1 through April 30 of the tax year, at the district or online. Bell CAD says no yearly renewal is needed unless the chief appraiser requests one or you change homes, and it takes late applications for two years after the tax goes delinquent.

Texas calls for a written notice to vacate, giving at least three days unless the lease sets a different period. Delivery options include hand delivery, leaving it inside the unit, mail, or email when the lease allows.

A tenant who stays faces a justice court case, with a hearing 10 to 21 days after filing. Appeals to county court must come within five days of judgment. How do foreclosure and tax liens reach a Belton house?

When a deed of trust grants power of sale, the lender can auction a Bell County house on a first Tuesday. The owner has 20 days after the default notice to reinstate, and the sale notice must go out 21 or more days beforehand.

By April 30 for the tax year. Bell CAD still takes late applications for up to two years after the tax turns delinquent, and no yearly renewal is required.

Yes, for certain entities. Bell CAD lists 3% in October, 2% in November and 1% in December, with the base amount due in January.

Only with a city permit. Belton requires one for every short-term rental, renewed yearly, and a non-owner-occupied rental must sit 500 feet from any other.

The owner on January 1 carries the lien and the liability. Sellers and buyers usually divide the bill at closing through the title company.

Bell CAD does, with offices in Belton, Killeen and Temple. The district says it normally reviews sales and properties every year.

Someone who buys and moves in can claim the exemption from the move-in date when the previous owner had none that year. The exemption also caps yearly appraisal growth at 10 percent, with exceptions for improvements and added land.

What is it like to sell a house in Kerrville?

Kerrville is a Hill Country city on the Guadalupe River, and the city calls itself the capital of the Texas Hill Country. Its founding dates to 1889, and the river runs straight through town.

Buyers come for the parks, golf courses and arts venues, and the city names Kerrville-Schreiner Park, Louise Hays Park and Flat Rock Park along the river. Schreiner University, the James Avery headquarters, the Museum of Western Art and the Kerrville Folk Festival are among the draws it lists. Houses close to the river carry both the appeal and the flood exposure, which now shapes how buyers and insurers view the area.

How did the July 2026 flood affect Kerrville homeowners?

The city has a recovery page for the July 2026 flood, and the state governor declared Kerr County a disaster area on July 17, 2026. If your house was damaged, that history will come up in any sale.

The deadline has passed, so a owner who missed it should call the appraisal district and ask whether any late option applies. The city page also lists debris collection, damage reporting through the state and a local disaster relief center. Several riverside parks and the River Trail were still reported closed on that page.

What should I do about flood or storm damage before selling?

Document it, repair or disclose it, and tell the title company what was claimed on insurance or through assistance programs.

  • Keep photos, contractor estimates and receipts for each damaged area.
  • Ask the city whether work needs a permit before a contractor begins.
  • Report damage through the state survey and the local recovery form so officials can track needs.
  • Ask Kerr Central Appraisal District how a temporary exemption affects the value on your account.

A cash buyer can purchase a damaged house as-is, which avoids mold remediation and drywall work on your end. Expect the price to reflect the repair scope.

Who appraises property in Kerr County?

Kerr Central Appraisal District, at 212 Oak Hollow Drive in Kerrville, appraises all real and business personal property in the county. It has online search, interactive maps, a forms page and an online protest portal.

It lists the taxing entities it serves, including Kerr County, the City of Kerrville, Kerrville ISD, Ingram ISD, Center Point ISD, the Upper Guadalupe River Authority and several emergency service districts. Your bill is a sum of several of those, so look at each line before assuming where the money goes.

How do Texas tax dates fit a Kerrville closing?

Value is set on January 1, the lien attaches that day, and bills go out in early October.

  • First half of a split bill: November 30. Second half: June 30.
  • Delinquent from February 1, with penalty and interest.
  • Homestead exemption filings are generally due April 30.
  • Protest deadline is generally May 15, or 30 days after the notice.

These dates come from the Comptroller's calendar. A seller closing mid-year normally credits the buyer for the unpaid part of the year at the closing table.

What are the ways to sell fast in Kerrville?

A flood-affected or older house changes which of three routes fits: listing, selling privately or a cash sale.

  • A listing suits a house in good shape on a fair timeline.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale cuts commission and puts disclosure on you.
  • A cash offer works for as-is houses, absentee owners and estate sales.

In a retirement-heavy Hill Country market, many sales also involve a move to be near family, so a firm closing date is often the deciding factor.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Kerrville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How is the deed recorded for a Kerr County property?

The Kerr County Clerk records deeds for land in the county, and an instrument must be signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer.

The Texas clerk manual lists a first-page fee of $5.00 and $4.00 for each added page, plus other records fees that vary by county. The title company handles filing, so ask for the final charges in your settlement statement.

Can a Kerrville seller use a transfer on death or land contract?

Texas lets an owner record a transfer on death deed so real property passes without probate, and a Lady Bird deed lets the owner keep selling or mortgaging the house without the beneficiary's consent. Either must be recorded in the county where the property sits, and the transfer on death deed has to be recorded before the owner dies.

A contract for deed is a different tool. Under Property Code chapter 5, the seller keeps title until the buyer finishes paying, and for a residence the buyer has a statutory right to cancel. Seller financing on a Kerrville house is possible, but the rules are strict, so have a Texas attorney draft it.

What do Kerrville buyers want to know about the river?

The Guadalupe River gives Kerrville its parks and its trail, and buyers ask which parts of town felt the July 2026 flood. The city's recovery page said Louise Hays Park, Lehmann-Monroe Park, Tranquility Island, Guadalupe Park and the River Trail were closed for flood damage, while Knapp Park and Cypress Park had reopened. Repair planning for the River Trail was underway.

If your house is on higher ground, say so and show the water history you know. If it took water, a cash buyer will price the repair, and a listing buyer will want inspection reports. Either way, accurate answers save time late in the deal.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Which schools and districts are in the Kerrville area?

Kerr CAD lists Kerrville ISD, Ingram ISD, Center Point ISD, Hunt ISD, Divide ISD, Comfort ISD, Medina ISD and Harper ISD among the taxing entities it appraises for. Your school district appears on your tax statement, and buyers check it first. The Upper Guadalupe River Authority and Headwaters Groundwater Conservation District also tax property here, so a Hill Country lot outside the city can carry more than one special district line.

Does Kerrville have a historic and cultural side that sellers can mention?

The city's own history notes German pioneers and the cowboys who started major cattle drives here on the Great Western Cattle Trail. It also lists the Official Texas State Arts and Crafts Fair, the Kerrville Folk Festival, the Museum of Western Art and venues such as The Point Theatre, the Kathleen C. Cailloux Theater and Schreiner University performances.

Festival weekends bring visitors, which helps a seller who offers a house with parking and guest space, and a house near a park trail will draw people who walk. Describe those features plainly. Buyers from out of the area often pick Kerrville for its mild climate and river access, so mention distance to the water, but also be honest about flood history.

What if I inherited a Kerrville house or owe back taxes?

For inherited property, Texas offers a will probate window of four years, muniment of title when no administration is needed, and a small estate affidavit for estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead.

On back taxes, the collector can add up to 20 percent attorney fees under a contract and can pursue a suit. Homestead owners may ask about a delinquent installment plan of up to 36 months where a collector allows it. Call the Kerr County tax office for a payoff figure.

More questions about Kerrville, TX

When was Kerrville founded?

The city's website says the community has thrived since its foundation in 1889.

Is the Kerrville flood property tax exemption still open?

No. The posted deadline was October 30, 2026, which has passed. Contact Kerr Central Appraisal District to ask whether a late option exists for your property.

What damage level qualified for the temporary exemption?

Kerr CAD said owners with at least 15 percent physical damage could apply, for property in an area the governor declared a disaster.

Where is the Kerr appraisal district office?

Kerr Central Appraisal District lists its office at 212 Oak Hollow Drive, Kerrville, Texas 78028. It also has a mailing address on its website.

Can I sell a flood-damaged house in Kerrville?

Yes, either as-is or after you repair it. Gather damage documentation, disclose what you know, and ask the city about permits before any rebuilding work.
